project.title: Beilinson–Bloch Heights and the Strong Zero-Curvature Green Conjecture
project.subtitle: Actual Green forms, canonical pairings, and arithmetic finiteness
project.summary: A research programme on strong non-Archimedean Green forms, Beilinson–Bloch height pairings, arithmetic Lefschetz theory, and integral Northcott properties.
project.motivation:
Heights measure the arithmetic size of geometric objects. On curves, degree-zero divisors lead to the Néron–Tate pairing on the Jacobian. In higher codimension, the corresponding pairing should connect algebraic cycles, local intersection theory, and arithmetic finiteness.

This programme separates three questions. Can one construct the local Green objects on the prescribed support complement? Can their local contributions be assembled into a canonical global pairing? Once a pairing is available, which positivity, nondegeneracy, and finiteness statements follow?

The local target is an actual Mihatsch \(\delta\)-form, not only a current. The arithmetic target counts images of integral cycles in rational Chow groups or their quotients. These choices determine the constructions and the obstructions studied here.
project.programme: The construction strand studies actual finite traces, support-preserving Green forms, numerical model certificates, and the image of the original Chow group in residual period spaces. The properties strand separates curve-visible abelian contributions from a residual Griffiths quotient. Arithmetic regulators, integral lattices, and fields of definition then provide distinct approaches to Northcott finiteness. A comparison strand connects normalized determinant metrics, local heights, and degeneration in families.

entries.title: The local actual-form problem
entries.summary: The original valued field, the precise support complement, and the full actual test class.
entries.statement:
Fix a finite extension \(K/\mathbf Q_p\) and its absolute value. Let \(X/K\) be smooth, projective and geometrically integral of dimension \(n\), and let \(Z\) be a rational cycle of codimension \(r\), with \(1\le r\le n\). Write \(U_Z=X^{\mathrm{an}}\setminus |Z|^{\mathrm{an}}\), retaining all components with nonzero coefficient. Let \(\mathcal B^{p,q}\) be the sheaf of ordinary actual Mihatsch \(\delta\)-forms and set \(D=d'd''\).

The Green identity is required for every \(\eta\in\mathcal B_c^{n-r,n-r}(X^{\mathrm{an}})\). The proposed construction must supply the integrability needed for its left-hand side. Finite extensions retain the given absolute value and the full field degree.

entries.title: Strong zero-curvature Green forms
entries.summary: Construct an actual Green form for every geometrically homologically trivial cycle.
entries.statement:
With the local data of BB-LOCAL-DATA, suppose that the geometric rational cycle class of \(Z\) is zero. There exists
\[
\gamma_Z\in\mathcal B^{r-1,r-1}(U_Z)
\]
such that all integrals below are defined and
\[
\int_{U_Z}\gamma_Z\wedge d'd''\eta=-\int_{Z^{\mathrm{an}}}\eta
\qquad\bigl(\eta\in\mathcal B_c^{n-r,n-r}(X^{\mathrm{an}})\bigr).
\]
The target is over the original valued field and on the complement of the specified cycle representative.

entries.approach: Construct supported Green pairs; identify their closed curvature obstruction; prove vanishing on the image of the original homologically trivial Chow group. Verify finite trace and descent on the full actual test class.

entries.title: A curve-normalized height system
entries.summary: The four explicit assumptions used by the height-properties theorems.
entries.statement:
Write \(V^r(X_E)=\operatorname{CH}^r(X_E)_{\mathrm{hom},\mathbf Q}\). For every smooth projective \(n\)-fold and every finite extension \(E/F\), assume pairings
\[
h_X:V^r(X_E)\times V^{n+1-r}(X_E)\longrightarrow\mathbf R
\]
satisfying: **H1**, rational bilinearity and symmetry in complementary degrees; **H2**, absolute-normalized extension invariance and isomorphism/Galois covariance; **H3**, full correspondence adjunction \(h_X(\Gamma_*z,w)=h_Y(z,{}^t\Gamma_*w)\); **H4**, on a pointed curve, \(-h_C\) is the positive Néron–Tate form for the canonical principal polarization in the matching Poincaré convention.
entries.motivation: This interface separates the arithmetic consequences of a pairing from the analytic problem of constructing it.

entries.title: A canonical global Beilinson–Bloch pairing
entries.summary: Assemble local contributions on the complete homologically trivial Chow groups.
entries.statement:
For every number field \(F\) and smooth projective geometrically integral \(X/F\) of dimension \(n\), construct a canonical real-valued pairing on
\[
\operatorname{CH}^r(X)_{\mathrm{hom},\mathbf Q}\times
\operatorname{CH}^{n+1-r}(X)_{\mathrm{hom},\mathbf Q}
\]
with the normalization and functoriality in BB-HEIGHT-DATA, agreeing with the classical Beilinson–Bloch pairing wherever the latter is defined. The construction includes convergence of the local sum and independence of representatives and auxiliary choices.

entries.motivation: Existence, positivity, and finiteness are separate questions. The first goal is a canonical pairing with the complete expected domain.
entries.approach: Use strong local Green identities together with local comparison, almost-everywhere compatibility, and the global product formula. A weaker intermediate target is vanishing of residual periods only on localizations of global Chow classes. For the H16 route, eliminate the localized global detector periods in both complementary codimensions and verify the assembly/comparison inputs at the relevant source version.

entries.title: Finite traces and exact-support Green pairs
entries.summary: The analytic interfaces that govern promotion of the current standalone draft.
entries.statement: Verify the finite-trace operator on the scalar–curvature module of actual forms: representation independence under all PL relations; compatibility with \(d'\), \(d''\), and the stated projection identities; the normalization by \([L:K]\); and extension of the integral identities to all actual compact tests. Verify the model-curvature numerical detector and the supported perfect-complex Green construction with their prescribed support and length multiplicities.
entries.approach: Recheck PL orbit sorting and parameter integration independently, then audit the model detector and finite-flat multisection argument. The analytic draft and its proof sources are provided as candidates for that review.

entries.title: Algebraic equivalence and compact parameters
entries.summary: A geometric deduction from a Chow-invariant actual obstruction and its support theorem.
entries.statement: Assume the Chow-invariant actual Bott–Chern obstruction and the exact-support Green-pair construction stated as (A1) and (A2) in the conditional transfer manuscript, together with its rational-fibre-rigidity input. Then, for every smooth projective \(X/K\), the obstruction vanishes on geometrically algebraically trivial rational cycles. Every prescribed representative of such a class therefore admits the zero-curvature Green form of STRONG-G.

source.publicationNote: Unsigned public copy; only personal attribution has been removed.

entries.proof: Generate algebraically trivial classes by curve correspondences and degree-zero divisors. The Poincaré family turns the obstruction into an additive map from a \(p\)-adic Jacobian. The actual-form parameter argument makes this map locally constant. A locally constant map from a compact \(p\)-adic group to a rational vector space has finite image; additivity and torsion-freeness force that image to be zero. The algebraic norm family on the Weil restriction has a rational fibre representing \([L:K]z\). Compact rigidity annihilates its obstruction, and rational linearity allows division by \([L:K]\). The full argument, including its analytic premises, is in the linked source.
entries.motivation: This isolates the geometric part of the algebraically trivial case from the finite-trace and actual-form foundations.

entries.title: Transfer through abelian Chow retracts
entries.summary: An actual diagonal factorization transports the abelian input.
entries.statement: Assume the analytic packages (A1), (A2), (N), and (C) of the conditional transfer manuscript. Suppose that after a finite extension, the diagonal of \(X\) admits a rational Chow factorization through abelian varieties with the required Tate shifts. Then every geometrically homologically trivial rational cycle on \(X\) admits the strong zero-curvature Green form on its prescribed complement.

source.publicationNote: Unsigned public copy; only personal attribution has been removed.

entries.proof: Use the abelian special-fibre numerical input to obtain the required obstruction vanishing on the source factors. Apply correspondence covariance to each term in the Chow identity \(\sum_j v_j\circ u_j=\Delta\). Their sum is the original Chow class. Finite-extension trace, with its full field-degree normalization, descends the vanishing. The support theorem then produces the form for the specified representative.
entries.motivation: The factorization must be an identity in the rational Chow category; a cohomological or numerical factorization alone does not supply this transfer.

entries.title: Actual Green forms on products of curves
entries.summary: The standalone draft combines finite traces, numerical liftings, and curve-motive decompositions.
entries.statement: Let \(K/\mathbf Q_p\) be finite, \(A/K\) an abelian variety, and \(C_1,\ldots,C_s\) smooth projective geometrically integral curves. Put \(X=A\times_K\prod_iC_i\). The expanded draft proposes strong G for every prescribed geometrically homologically trivial rational cycle of codimension \(1\le r\le\dim X\). Its proof uses the separate Chow diagonal, simultaneous regular-model construction, and model-sensitive numerical transfer recorded below.

source.publicationNote: Unsigned public copy; only personal attribution has been removed.

entries.proof: Split each pointed curve motive as \(\mathbf1\oplus h^1(C_i)\oplus\mathbb L\), realize \(h^1(C_i)\) through its Jacobian, and tensor the decompositions to obtain actual diagonal factorizations. Numerical model certificates are transported by refined intersection and the projection formula. The proposed analytic trace, detector, and supported Green constructions then connect those certificates to actual forms. All six proof-source files are preserved in the source edition.
entries.approach: The immediate review targets are finite-trace representation independence, PL parameter integration, the numerical curvature detector, and exact-support perfect-complex realization.

entries.title: Integral images and bounded-degree Northcott
entries.summary: Count geometric classes with integral representatives, not all rational multiples.
entries.statement:
Fix an algebraic closure \(\overline F\). Let \(\Lambda_X^r(E)\) be the image of integral-coefficient cycles over \(E\) with zero geometric rational cycle class in \(V^r(X_{\overline F})\). For a fixed rational projector use its projected integral image; for a quotient use the image of that subgroup.

A quadratic form \(q\) has bounded-degree Northcott if, for every \(B\in\mathbf R\) and integer \(D\ge1\),
\[
\left\{\xi\in\bigcup_{[E:F]\le D}\Lambda(E):q(\xi)\le B\right\}
\]
is finite. Fixed-field Northcott fixes \(E\) instead.
entries.motivation: A rational vector space admits arbitrarily small rational multiples of a nonzero vector. An arithmetic finiteness statement therefore needs an integral image or a fixed denominator bound.

entries.title: Pointed products and central residual groups
entries.summary: The all-h¹ core and its algebraic and Griffiths parts.
entries.statement:
Let \(F\) be a number field, fix an embedding \(\overline F\hookrightarrow\mathbf C\), and let each basepoint \(o_i\in C_i(F)\) be rational over \(F\). Homological and algebraic triviality are geometric, after base change to \(\overline F\). All \(E/F\) below are finite. Write \(V^r=\operatorname{CH}^r_{\mathrm{hom},\mathbf Q}\).

Let \(X=\prod_{i=1}^nC_i\) be a product of smooth projective pointed curves with points \(o_i\). Put \(\pi_{1,i}=\Delta_{C_i}-o_i\times C_i-C_i\times o_i\) and \(\ell=\sum_i a_i p_i^*[o_i]\), where \(a_i\in\mathbf Z_{>0}\). For a subproduct \(Y_S\), set
\[
\Pi_S=\bigotimes_{i\in S}\pi_{1,i},\qquad U_S^c(E)=\Pi_{S*}\operatorname{CH}^c(Y_{S,E})_{\mathrm{hom},\mathbf Q}.
\]
The core is central when \(|S|=2c-1\). In that case write \(U_E=U_S^c(E)\), \(A_E=U_E\cap\operatorname{CH}^c(Y_{S,E})_{\mathrm{alg},\mathbf Q}\), and \(G_E=U_E/A_E\).

For \(1\le r\le\lfloor(n+1)/2\rfloor\), the arithmetic primitive subspace is
\[
P^r_\ell=\ker\!\left(\ell^{n+2-2r}:V^r(X_E)\longrightarrow V^{n+2-r}(X_E)\right).
\]

entries.title: Off-central Chow vanishing
entries.summary: Only the arithmetic middle degree should survive in the all-h¹ homological kernel.
entries.statement:
For every subproduct \(Y_S\), every finite extension \(E/F_0\), and every codimension \(c\) with \(|S|\ne2c-1\),
\[
U_S^c(E)=0.
\]
Here \(F_0\) is one fixed field defining the projectors under consideration.

references.locator: Conjecture 2.3.1; 2022 version
references.description: Arithmetic Lefschetz and Hodge-type structures provide the conjectural background for the product-of-curves reductions.

entries.motivation: The exact Chow-block decomposition turns this vanishing into the arithmetic hard Lefschetz condition for the anchored product polarization.
entries.approach: Study the original all-h¹ Chow source on each subproduct. Isolate the noncentral projector pieces rather than asking only for vanishing of their ordinary cohomology.

entries.title: Central algebraic Abel–Jacobi injectivity
entries.summary: Eliminate the algebraic contribution to the height radical.
entries.statement: For every odd subproduct \(|S|=2c-1\) and every finite extension \(E/F_0\), the rationalized complex Abel–Jacobi map is injective on \(A_{S,E}\). Its target is \(J^c(Y_{S,\mathbf C})(\mathbf C)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q\).
entries.motivation: Under the height axioms, this kernel is exactly the algebraic part of the full central height radical.

entries.title: Residual integral Northcott
entries.summary: Bounded height and bounded field degree should leave finitely many residual cycle classes.
entries.statement: Assume the height system H1–H4. For every odd subproduct \(|S|=2c-1\), let \(h_{G,S}\) be the orthogonalized residual pairing and \(q_{G,S}(\xi)=(-1)^c h_{G,S}(\xi,\xi)\). Then \(q_{G,S}\) has bounded-degree Northcott on the projected integral image \(\Lambda_{G,S}\).
entries.motivation: This conjecture contains real positive definiteness, but also asks for arithmetic discreteness and control of fields of definition.
entries.approach: Combine residual rational detection, a common integral lattice or height gap, and bounded ramification of minimal class fields.

entries.title: Real positivity on the residual Griffiths quotient
entries.summary: A weaker target than residual integral Northcott.
entries.statement: Assume H1–H4. For each fixed finite \(E/F_0\), the form \(q_G(\xi)=(-1)^c h_G(\xi,\xi)\) is positive definite after extending scalars to \(G_E\otimes_{\mathbf Q}\mathbf R\).
entries.motivation: Positivity detects a real radical. Integral Northcott additionally excludes dense denominator structures; R2-N2 proves the implication from finiteness to real positivity.

entries.title: Arithmetic Lefschetz from off-central vanishing
entries.summary: An unconditional equivalence in the actual Chow group of a pointed product.
entries.statement:
For the pointed product and anchored polarization in BB-CENTRAL-DATA, over each fixed finite \(E/F\), off-central vanishing on every subproduct is equivalent to the isomorphisms
\[
\ell^{n+1-2r}:V^r(X_E)\xrightarrow{\sim}V^{n+1-r}(X_E),\qquad 1\le r\le\lfloor(n+1)/2\rfloor.
\]
The statement is an equivalence of properties; it does not assume either side has been established for a general product.

references.label: Shou-Wu Zhang — Standard Conjectures and Height Pairings
references.locator: Conjecture 2.3.1; 2022 version
references.description: Arithmetic Lefschetz and Hodge-type structures provide the conjectural background for the product-of-curves reductions.

entries.proof:
The curve projectors give the exact decomposition
\[
V^*(X_E)=\bigoplus_{S,c}U_S^c(E)\otimes B_I[c],\qquad B_I=\mathbf Q[x_i:i\in I]/(x_i^2),\quad I=[n]\setminus S.
\]
Under \(u\otimes x_T\mapsto (\prod_{i\in T}a_i)j_Tu\), multiplication by \(\ell\) is multiplication by \(E_I=\sum_{i\in I}x_i\). The square-zero algebra has the standard Lefschetz strings, so \(E_I^{m-2t}:B_I^t\to B_I^{m-t}\) is an isomorphism for \(0\le t\le m/2\).

If \(k=|S|=2c-1\), the arithmetic exponent is \(n+1-2r=m-2t\), with \(t=r-c\). Thus central blocks satisfy the desired isomorphisms. Conversely, for a nonzero block put \(d=k+1-2c\). If \(d>0\), choose \(r=c\): the power \(m+d\) kills \(U_S^c\otimes1\), contradicting injectivity. If \(d<0\), choose \(r=k+1-c\): the source has polynomial degree \(d<0\), whereas the target contains \(U_S^c\otimes x_I\), contradicting surjectivity. Hence all surviving blocks are central.

entries.title: The primitive sum-of-squares identity
entries.summary: An exact factorial and sign identify primitive heights with central heights.
entries.statement:
Assume H1–H4. Let \(|S|=2c-1\), \(m=n-|S|\), and \(0\le t=r-c\le m/2\). In the weighted Chow block write \(z_S=\sum_{|T|=t}u_Tx_T\). It is primitive precisely when \(Fz_S=0\), where \(Fx_T=\sum_{i\in T}x_{T\setminus\{i\}}\). Then
\[
(-1)^rh_X(z_S,\ell^{n+1-2r}z_S)
=(m-2t)!\!\prod_{i\notin S}a_i\sum_{|T|=t}(-1)^ch_{Y_S}(u_T,u_T).
\]
The common integer \(N_a=\prod_i a_i\) clears all coefficient denominators, independently of the cycle and finite field extension.
entries.proof:
Let \(*x_T=x_{I\setminus T}\). The relations \([F,E]=H\), with \(Hx_T=(m-2|T|)x_T\), identify primitive vectors with \(\ker F\). For a primitive vector, the coefficient sums over \(T\supset J\) vanish when \(|J|<t\). Inclusion–exclusion then gives
\[
E^{m-2t}z_S=(-1)^t(m-2t)!*z_S.
\]
Correspondence adjunction makes complementary point/fundamental-class indices pair, and all other indices vanish. Each surviving weight is \(a_Ta_{I\setminus T}=\prod_{i\in I}a_i\). Finally \((-1)^{r+t}=(-1)^c\). The coefficient map divides by \(a_T\), and every \(a_T\) divides \(N_a\).
entries.motivation: Central real positivity yields primitive positivity and Cauchy–Schwarz. With off-central vanishing and central integral Northcott over all finite extensions, the uniform denominator also propagates bounded-degree finiteness.

dependencyNotes.R2-L1: Uses the Chow-block decomposition and square-zero algebra in its proof. Off-central vanishing and the hard-Lefschetz equivalence are not premises of the central-block identity.

entries.title: The maximal curve-visible Chow projector
entries.summary: An actual idempotent separates a fixed abelian summand from the residual motive.
entries.statement:
For a central product \(Y\) with \(\Pi=\bigotimes\pi_{1,i}\), after one fixed finite extension \(F_0/F\) there are actual rational Chow idempotents
\[
e={}^te=e^2,\quad e\Pi=\Pi e=e,\quad R=\Pi-e.
\]
The cohomological image of \(e\) is the span of all curve-correspondence \(H^1\)-images in \(\Pi H^{2c-1}(Y)\), and \(eU_E\simeq B(E)_{\mathbf Q}\) through fixed Chow correspondences for a fixed abelian variety \(B/F_0\).

The identification with \(B(E)_{\mathbf Q}\) holds for every finite \(E/F_0\).
entries.proof: Choose finitely many curve correspondences \(\Gamma\) spanning the indicated finite-dimensional cohomological space. Set \(a={}^t\Gamma\Gamma\) in the endomorphism algebra of the sum of their \(h^1\)-motives. Hodge–Riemann makes \((-1)^{c-1}a\) positive semidefinite and identifies its kernel with that of \(\Gamma\). A rational polynomial gives \(a^+\), inverse on the nonzero spectrum and zero on the kernel. Faithfulness of the \(h^1\) realization makes \(e=\Gamma a^+{}^t\Gamma\) an actual Chow idempotent. The corresponding abelian isogeny factor is the image of \(a^+a\).
entries.motivation: This construction does not use the conjectural actual Green-form height construction.

entries.title: The algebraic radical and residual pairing
entries.summary: Orthogonalize before passing to the Griffiths quotient.
entries.statement:
Assume H1–H4 and use the projectors in BB-CHOW-PROJECTOR. Then \(U_E=eU_E\oplus RU_E\) is height-orthogonal, the signed form on \(eU_E\) is a positive Néron–Tate form, and
\[
RA_E=\ker(\mathrm{AJ}_{\mathbf Q}|_{A_E})
=A_E\cap\operatorname{rad}(h|_{U_E})
=\operatorname{rad}(h|_{A_E}).
\]
The induced form on \(RU_E/RA_E\simeq G_E\) is independent of the chosen maximal curve-visible projector; denote it by \(h_G\).
entries.proof: A curve correspondence with zero \(H^1\)-action has transpose zero on complementary homologically trivial cycles: Abel–Jacobi functoriality reduces this to the faithful Picard group of the source curve. Adjunction therefore makes its image a height-radical subspace. Maximality of the visible summand applies this argument to \(RA_E\). On \(eU_E\), Abel–Jacobi has finite kernel and the signed height is nondegenerate. This proves the kernel equalities. Two orthogonalized lifts of a Griffiths class differ by an element of the full radical, proving independence.
entries.motivation: The original pairing does not directly descend through the algebraically trivial subgroup: its curve-visible part carries a nonzero Néron–Tate pairing.

entries.title: The exact central Northcott criterion
entries.summary: Central finiteness is equivalent to algebraic AJ injectivity plus residual finiteness.
entries.statement: Assume H1–H4. The central form \(q_U(z)=(-1)^ch_Y(z,z)\) has bounded-degree Northcott on \(\Lambda_U\) if and only if \(\ker(\mathrm{AJ}_{\mathbf Q}|_{A_E})=0\) for every finite \(E/F_0\) and \(q_G\) has bounded-degree Northcott on \(\Lambda_G\). The same equivalence holds over a fixed field.
entries.proof:
A nonzero algebraic radical class can be multiplied into the integral image; all its integer multiples have height zero, contradicting finiteness. Choose a fixed integer \(M\) clearing the denominator of \(R\). An integral lift \(z\) of \(\xi\in\Lambda_G(E)\) gives \(MRz\in\Lambda_U(E)\), with \(q_U(MRz)=M^2q_G(\xi)\) and quotient class \(M\xi\). Thus central Northcott implies residual Northcott.

Conversely, residual Northcott forces nonnegativity on all rational residual classes by the multiples argument. Orthogonality gives \(q_U(z)=q_e(ez)+q_G([z])\). The residual class \([z]\) has finitely many possibilities at bounded height and degree. A fixed curve correspondence detects \(ez\) in a Jacobian, after one common denominator; classical Néron–Tate Northcott bounds the first component. The map \(z\mapsto(ez,[z])\) is injective exactly when the algebraic AJ kernel vanishes.

entries.title: Northcott forces real positivity
entries.summary: Finiteness excludes real null directions, even without a finite-rank assumption.
entries.statement: Let \(\Lambda\) be an additive subgroup spanning a rational vector space \(V\), and let \(q\) be a real-valued quadratic form. If every upper height ball on \(\Lambda\) is finite, the scalar extension of \(q\) to \(V\otimes_{\mathbf Q}\mathbf R\) is positive definite.
entries.proof:
Restrict to any finite-dimensional rational subspace and choose a basis in \(\Lambda\). A negative real direction for its Gram matrix \(Q\) gives a negative rational direction by approximation. Clearing denominators yields a nonzero integral vector whose multiples contradict Northcott. Hence \(Q\) is positive semidefinite.

If \(0\ne u\in\ker Q\), round \(tu\) to integral coordinate vectors \(z_t\). Their errors are uniformly bounded, and \(q(z_t)=(z_t-tu)^tQ(z_t-tu)\) is bounded. But the vectors \(z_t\) are unbounded and therefore take infinitely many values. This contradiction proves positivity on every finite-dimensional real extension, which proves the assertion.
entries.motivation: Northcott is stronger than positivity alone. It need not force finite rational rank: weighted orthogonal sums can have finite balls and infinite rank.

entries.title: An equivalent package for products of curves
entries.summary: The geometric, radical, and integral conjectures assemble into one exact equivalence.
entries.statement:
Assume H1–H4 for a fixed pointed product and its anchored polarization. The following packages are equivalent:

1. Arithmetic hard Lefschetz holds in every relevant degree over every finite extension, and every primitive integral image has bounded-degree Northcott for \(q_{\ell,r}\).
2. Off-central vanishing holds on all subproducts; the algebraic rational Abel–Jacobi kernel vanishes on every odd central core; every residual integral image satisfies bounded-degree Northcott.

Either package implies real primitive positivity and nondegeneracy of the complementary pairings over each fixed number field.

references.label: Shou-Wu Zhang — Standard Conjectures and Height Pairings
references.locator: Conjecture 2.3.1; 2022 version
references.description: Arithmetic Lefschetz and Hodge-type structures provide the conjectural background for the product-of-curves reductions.

entries.proof:
From (2), R2-L1 gives hard Lefschetz, R2-N1 gives central integral Northcott, and R2-N2 gives real central positivity. The sum-of-squares identity and its fixed coefficient denominator propagate positivity and Northcott to the primitive groups.

Conversely, hard Lefschetz gives off-central vanishing. Inflate a central class \(u\) by fundamental classes on omitted factors. This is an integral primitive injection \(j_{\varnothing}\) in degree \(c\), with height \(m!\prod_{i\notin S}a_i\,q_{S,c}(u)\). Primitive Northcott therefore gives central Northcott, and R2-N1 supplies the other two assertions in (2).

entries.title: The residual arithmetic regulator
entries.summary: An actual Chow projector yields a regulator on the Griffiths quotient.
entries.statement:
For a central residual projector \(R\), put \(V_p=R_*H^{2c-1}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(Y_{\overline F},\mathbf Q_p(c))\). There is a canonical arithmetic regulator
\[
a_{p,E}:G_E\longrightarrow H^1(E,V_p),
\]
independent of the curve-visible lift under the common cohomological identification. No height axioms are needed for this construction.

references.label: Wayne Raskind — Higher ℓ-adic Abel–Jacobi mappings and filtrations on Chow groups
references.locator: Proposition 2.5 and Corollary 2.6
references.description: Arithmetic cycle classes and Hochschild–Serre filtrations form part of the residual regulator background.

references.label: Bruno Kahn — On the injectivity and non-injectivity of the ℓ-adic cycle class maps
references.locator: Theorem 2.4; source version recorded in Round 2
references.description: The integral cycle-image finiteness input used in the local lattice argument.

entries.proof: The actual central projector leaves a single geometric cohomology row. In total degree \(2c\), its Hochschild–Serre filtration has \(F^1=H\) and \(F^2=0\), giving the required edge map. Curve-generated algebraically trivial classes map to zero because \(R\) kills their \(H^1\)-images. Restriction–corestriction descends this vanishing from a finite field of definition. Thus the map factors through \(G_E\).

entries.title: Weight −1 and finite-dimensional arithmetic targets
entries.summary: The full rational cohomological target is controlled over each fixed field.
entries.statement:
For the representation \(V_p\) in R2-R1, let \(S_E\) contain the archimedean places, places above \(p\), and the places of a fixed bad-reduction set. Then
\[
H^1(G_{E,S_E},V_p)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^1(E,V_p)
\]
is finite-dimensional. For a stable free \(\mathbf Z_p\)-lattice, the corresponding global \(H^1\) is finitely generated. At good finite places away from \(p\), \(H^1(E_v,V_p)=0\).

references.label: J. S. Milne — Arithmetic Duality Theorems
references.locator: Second edition, Corollary I.4.15 and Proposition I.0.22(c)
references.description: Finiteness and continuous arithmetic cohomology used in the weight-minus-one target.

entries.proof: Purity gives weight \(-1\), so neither Frobenius on \(V_p\) nor the inertia-invariant term \(V_p(-1)\) has eigenvalue one at a good place away from \(p\). Local rational \(H^1\) vanishes. The cocycle calculation then factors global classes through the quotient unramified outside \(S_E\). Finiteness for finite coefficient modules, inverse limits, and compact Nakayama give integral finite generation and rational finite dimension.
entries.motivation: This controls cohomology over a chosen field. It does not bound the ramification of the fields of definition as those fields vary.

entries.title: Local integral images of residual regulators
entries.summary: For each coefficient prime, integral residual cycle images lie in a finite module.
entries.statement: For each fixed \(E\) and prime \(p\), \(a_{p,E}(\Lambda_G(E))\) lies in a finitely generated \(\mathbf Z_p\)-module. If the scalar-extended map \(G_E\otimes_{\mathbf Q}\mathbf Q_p\to H^1(E,V_p)\) is injective, then \(G_E\) has finite rational dimension, \(\Lambda_G(E)\otimes\mathbf Z_p\) is finitely generated, and \(\Lambda_G(E)/p\Lambda_G(E)\) is finite.

references.label: Bruno Kahn — On the injectivity and non-injectivity of the ℓ-adic cycle class maps
references.locator: Theorem 2.4; source version recorded in Round 2
references.description: The integral cycle-image finiteness input used in the local lattice argument.

entries.proof: Clear the denominator of the fixed Chow projector. Apply the integral continuous cycle-image bound, intersect its rational image with the residual summand, and only then use the one-row edge map. This gives the finite integral target. Under the explicitly stated scalar-injectivity hypothesis, tensoring the integral-image map with \(\mathbf Z_p\) embeds the tensor lattice into that finite module.
entries.motivation: The scalar-injectivity condition in the second assertion is an open geometric input. Mere rational linear injectivity into a p-adic space is insufficient.

entries.title: Residual rational detection
entries.summary: Injectivity must survive extension of scalars to the coefficient field.
entries.statement:
For every finite \(E/F_0\) and every prime \(p\), the residual regulator induces an injection
\[
G_E\otimes_{\mathbf Q}\mathbf Q_p\hookrightarrow H^1(E,V_p).
\]

references.label: Wayne Raskind — Higher ℓ-adic Abel–Jacobi mappings and filtrations on Chow groups
references.locator: Proposition 2.5 and Corollary 2.6
references.description: Arithmetic cycle classes and Hochschild–Serre filtrations form part of the residual regulator background.

references.label: Bruno Kahn — On the injectivity and non-injectivity of the ℓ-adic cycle class maps
references.locator: Theorem 2.4; source version recorded in Round 2
references.description: The integral cycle-image finiteness input used in the local lattice argument.

entries.motivation: Together with the finite-dimensional cohomological target, this would give finite rational rank and local integral control.

entries.title: Residual integral discreteness
entries.summary: A single rational lattice should control all integral residual classes over a fixed field.
entries.statement:
For every finite \(E/F_0\), the space \(G_E\) is finite-dimensional and there are a rational basis \(v_1,\ldots,v_s\) and \(N_E\ge1\) such that
\[
\Lambda_G(E)\subseteq N_E^{-1}\sum_i\mathbf Z v_i.
\]
entries.approach: Prove almost-everywhere saturation of regulator inverse lattices relative to one rational lattice, or combine a genuine positive height gap with finite Kummer quotients.

entries.title: Five equivalent lattice conditions
entries.summary: Finite-rank Northcott is exactly a discreteness condition.
entries.statement: Let \(\Lambda\) be torsion-free of finite rank, \(V=\Lambda\otimes\mathbf Q\), and let \(q\) be positive definite on \(V\otimes\mathbf R\). The following are equivalent: Northcott on \(\Lambda\); a positive lower bound for \(q\) on nonzero elements; finite generation of \(\Lambda\); containment in \(N^{-1}\Lambda_0\) for a rational full lattice \(\Lambda_0\); and relative compactness of the diagonal image in \(V(\mathbf A_f)\).
entries.proof: Finiteness of the unit ball supplies a positive gap. The gap makes \(\Lambda\) uniformly discrete in its finite-dimensional Euclidean space. Reducing modulo the span of a rational basis in \(\Lambda\) puts every coset representative in a bounded parallelepiped, so only finitely many occur. Thus that span has finite index and the denominators are bounded. Conversely, bounded subsets of a Euclidean lattice are finite. Finally, finite-adelic compact subsets lie in \(N^{-1}\Lambda_0\otimes\widehat{\mathbf Z}\) for some \(N\); intersection with the rational vector space gives the denominator criterion.

entries.title: An all-prime saturation criterion
entries.summary: Local integral detectors yield a global denominator when they agree almost everywhere.
entries.statement:
Let \(V\) be finite-dimensional over \(\mathbf Q\), \(\Lambda_0\) a full lattice, and \(\Lambda\subset V\). Suppose for every prime \(p\) there is an injective map \(D_p:V\otimes\mathbf Q_p\to W_p\) and a full lattice \(M_p\subset W_p\), with
\[
D_p(\Lambda)\subseteq M_p,\qquad D_p^{-1}(M_p)=\Lambda_0\otimes\mathbf Z_p
\quad\text{for almost every }p.
\]
Then \(\Lambda\subseteq N^{-1}\Lambda_0\) for one integer \(N\), and every real positive definite quadratic form has Northcott on \(\Lambda\).
entries.proof: Each inverse lattice \(D_p^{-1}(M_p)\) is open and compact by injectivity. At each exceptional prime choose \(b_p\) bounding it by \(p^{-b_p}\Lambda_0\otimes\mathbf Z_p\). Set \(N=\prod p^{b_p}\). Every rational coordinate of \(N\lambda\) is integral in every \(\mathbf Z_p\), hence belongs to \(\mathbf Z\). Apply R2-N3.
entries.motivation: The almost-everywhere equality with one common rational lattice is precisely the extra input still needed for the residual regulators.

entries.title: Weak Mordell–Weil and a positive height gap
entries.summary: A quantitative descent criterion without a prior finite-rank assumption.
entries.statement:
Let \(\Lambda\) be torsion-free and let \(\sqrt q\) be a real positive quadratic norm on \(\Lambda\otimes\mathbf R\). Suppose \(s=|\Lambda/m\Lambda|<\infty\) for some integer \(m\ge2\), and \(q(\lambda)\ge\varepsilon>0\) for every nonzero \(\lambda\). Then \(\Lambda\) is finitely generated and has Northcott. For \(B\ge0\) and integer \(j\ge0\) with \(m^{2j}\varepsilon>4B\),
\[
\#\{\lambda:q(\lambda)\le B\}\le s^j.
\]
entries.proof: If \(x,y\) have height at most \(B\) and \(x-y=m^jz\), then \(\|z\|\le2\sqrt B/m^j<\sqrt\varepsilon\), so \(z=0\). The height ball injects into \(\Lambda/m^j\Lambda\), whose size is \(s^j\). Choose finitely many representatives \(T\) modulo \(m\Lambda\) and write \(x=my+t\). The inequality \(\|y\|\le(\|x\|+\max_T\|t\|)/m\) descends into a fixed finite ball. That ball together with \(T\) generates \(\Lambda\).

entries.title: Why p-adic finiteness alone is not Northcott
entries.summary: An abstract denominator example isolates a missing global condition.
entries.statement: The group \(\Lambda=\sum_{p\ \mathrm{prime}}\mathbf Z\,p^{-1}\subset\mathbf Q\), with \(q(x)=x^2\), has \(\Lambda\otimes\mathbf Z_p=p^{-1}\mathbf Z_p\) at every prime, yet fails Northcott. This is an example of abstract groups, not a counterexample to a geometric conjecture.
entries.proof: All denominators are squarefree. After tensoring with \(\mathbf Z_p\), all denominators away from \(p\) become units, and the remaining factor gives \(p^{-1}\mathbf Z_p\). Nevertheless the distinct elements \(1/p\) satisfy \(q(1/p)=1/p^2\to0\). Thus finite generation at each coefficient prime gives no single global denominator bound.

entries.title: Trace to the field of a cycle class
entries.summary: The descent multiplier is the relative field degree.
entries.statement:
Let \(\mathcal G\) be a rational geometric Chow quotient with its discrete Galois action and compatible integral images preserved by restriction and trace. For \(\xi\in\Lambda(E)\), let \(K=F_0(\xi)\) be the fixed field of its stabilizer. Then
\[
K\subseteq E,\qquad [E:K]\xi\in\Lambda(K).
\]
If \([E:F_0]\le D\), the multiplier is at most \(D\).
entries.proof: The Galois group of \(\overline F/E\) fixes \(\xi\), hence \(K\subseteq E\). Push an integral representative over \(E\) down to \(K\). Over the algebraic closure its class is the sum over the \(K\)-embeddings of \(E\), and every summand equals \(\xi\). Fixed projectors commute with trace and algebraic equivalence is preserved by it.

entries.title: Ramification is the remaining variable-field condition
entries.summary: Fixed-field Northcott plus finite ramification sets is equivalent to bounded-degree Northcott.
entries.statement: Assume a Galois-invariant quadratic form \(q\) has fixed-field Northcott on \(\Lambda(K)\) for every finite \(K/F_0\). Then bounded-degree Northcott is equivalent to this condition: for every \(B\ge0,D\ge1\), the minimal class fields of all \(\xi\in\Lambda(E)\) with \([E:F_0]\le D\) and \(q(\xi)\le B\) are unramified outside one finite set \(S(B,D)\).

references.label: Kiran Kedlaya — Weil cohomology in practice
references.locator: Chapter 10: Comparing Galois representations: the Faltings–Serre method; Theorem 10.2.2
references.description: The finite-ramification form of Hermite–Minkowski used to control minimal class fields.

entries.proof: A degree bound and a fixed ramification set leave finitely many fields by Hermite–Minkowski. R2-F1 gives \(m\xi\in\Lambda(K)\), with \(1\le m\le D\) and \(q(m\xi)\le D^2B\). Fixed-field Northcott yields finitely many \(m\xi\); multiplication by \(m\) is injective in a rational group. Conversely, a finite height ball has finitely many class fields, and their ramified places form a finite set.

entries.title: Ramification of residual class fields
entries.summary: Bound the places of ramification as both the cycle class and its field vary.
entries.statement: Assume H1–H4. For every \(B\ge0,D\ge1\), there is a finite set of places of \(F_0\), depending on \(Y,\Pi,B,D\), outside which all minimal fields \(F_0(\xi)\) are unramified, for \(\xi\in\Lambda_G(E)\) with \([E:F_0]\le D\) and \(q_G(\xi)\le B\).
entries.motivation: Once fixed-field Northcott is known, R2-F2 identifies this as exactly the missing bounded-degree condition.

entries.title: A quantitative discriminant bound
entries.summary: A stronger route from height to control of the class field.
entries.statement:
For each fixed degree bound \(D\), do constants \(A_D,B_D\) exist such that every integral residual class of degree at most \(D\) satisfies
\[
\log N_{F_0/\mathbf Q}\mathfrak d_{F_0(\xi)/F_0}\le A_Dq_G(\xi)+B_D?
\]
The discriminant ideal is that of the minimal field of the geometric class.
entries.motivation: This asks for a quantitative inequality stronger than the qualitative ramification conjecture.

entries.title: An exact normalized Quillen isometry
entries.summary: Origin normalization removes the constant in a determinant comparison.
entries.statement:
Let \(C\) be a pointed smooth projective connected complex curve, \(J=\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)\), and \(\mathcal P\) its axis-rigidified Poincaré bundle with its standard smooth metric: the axis units have norm one and the curvature is purely mixed. Let \(X\) be smooth projective connected, \(M=C\times X\), \(q:M\to C\), and \(\mathcal F\) a hermitian perfect complex. Choose fixed product Kähler metrics and hermitian vector-bundle representatives. In the cochain determinant convention define
\[
\mathscr D_M(\mathcal F)=\det Rp_{J*}(\mathcal P_M\otimes\mathcal F_J)\otimes\bigl(\det R\Gamma(M,\mathcal F)\otimes\mathcal O_J\bigr)^{-1}.
\]
Define \(\mathscr D_C(K)\) in the same way on \(C\times J\). Each constant denominator carries the Quillen norm of the same complex and metrics as the numerator at the origin. Then derived projection gives an exact rigidified isometry on all of \(J\):
\[
\mathscr D_M(\mathcal F)\simeq\mathscr D_C(Rq_*\mathcal F).
\]

references.label: Bismut–Gillet–Soulé — Analytic torsion and holomorphic determinant bundles I
references.locator: Theorem 0.1, with the determinant convention fixed in the manuscript
references.description: The family index formula supplies the curvature calculation for normalized Quillen determinants.

entries.proof: Derived projection gives the algebraic rigidified isomorphism. Write \(\Omega=c_1(\overline{\mathcal P})\); its bidegree is purely mixed between \(C\) and \(J\). In the family index formula only \(\Omega^2/2\) contributes to the base degree two, and both normalized determinants have curvature \(\tfrac12\operatorname{rk}(Rq_*\mathcal F)\int_C\Omega^2\). Their norm ratio is a smooth pluriharmonic function on the compact Jacobian, hence constant. The origin rigidification has norm one on both sides, making the constant one.

entries.title: Rank zero, Deligne pairings, and filtered Riemann–Roch
entries.summary: The determinant metric becomes the flat Poincaré metric of a divisor class.
entries.statement:
In the normalized complex setup of R2-M1, a virtual-rank-zero perfect complex \(K\) on \(C\) has a unique rigidified isometry
\[
\mathscr D_C(K)\simeq\langle\mathcal P,p_C^*\det K\rangle_{C\times J/J}.
\]
For the cycle comparison, let \(\dim X=n\), \(\Gamma\in\operatorname{CH}^r(C\times X)_{\mathbf Q}\), and \(W\in\operatorname{CH}^{n+1-r}(X)_{\mathrm{hom},\mathbf Q}\). Choose rational \(K_0\)-lifts \(E_\Gamma,E_W\) whose Chern characters begin with these cycles in their indicated codimensions, and put
\[
\mathcal F=E_\Gamma\otimes^{\mathbf L}p_X^*E_W,\qquad K=Rq_*\mathcal F.
\]
Filtered Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch gives
\[
\operatorname{rk}K=0,\qquad c_1(\det K)=q_*(\Gamma\cdot p_X^*W)={}^t\Gamma_*W\quad\text{in }\operatorname{CH}^1(C)_{\mathbf Q}.
\]
The divisor class has degree zero, and the resulting normalized determinant has the flat Poincaré metric attached to that class.

references.label: Sergey Gorchinskiy — Notes on the biextension of Chow groups
references.locator: Determinant-of-cohomology and biextension comparisons
references.description: Connects several constructions of the Chow-group biextension, including determinant of cohomology.

references.label: Bismut–Gillet–Soulé — Analytic torsion and holomorphic determinant bundles I
references.locator: Theorem 0.1, with the determinant convention fixed in the manuscript
references.description: The family index formula supplies the curvature calculation for normalized Quillen determinants.

entries.proof: On a smooth curve, the rank-zero class is \([\det K]-[\mathcal O]\). Determinant identities identify the line with the Deligne pairing. Both normalized metrics are flat and have unit norm at the origin, so the rigidified isomorphism is an isometry. For the cycle statement, the top filtered Chern character has codimension \(n+1\) on \(C\times X\); pushforward gives the transposed divisor class. Common tensor powers clear rational denominators, and taking the positive metric root fixes the rational line.
entries.motivation: This is a scoped determinant/GRR comparison. Identifying it with a Green-form height additionally requires the corresponding metric and biextension comparison.

entries.title: Good-reduction determinant metrics
entries.summary: A smooth source model fixes the non-Archimedean metric exactly.
entries.statement: Let \(\mathcal C\) be a smooth proper geometrically connected curve over a complete DVR, with a section, and let its Jacobian be an abelian scheme. Use the absolute value inducing this DVR valuation. For a perfect complex \(K\) on \(\mathcal C\) with generic virtual rank zero and determinant degree zero, the origin-normalized determinant model metric agrees with the canonical rigidified Poincaré metric. Any ambient derived pushforward is assumed perfect.
entries.proof: On the generic fibre the rigidified determinant and Poincaré lines agree. Their model quotient is represented by a vertical divisor. The special fibre of the abelian scheme is integral, so this divisor is a multiple of that fibre. The integral zero-section rigidification forces the multiple to vanish. Normality extends the resulting isomorphism, and equality of model metrics follows.

entries.title: Bad-reduction metric compatibility
entries.summary: Determine the correction that connects semistable model determinants to actual Green heights.
entries.statement: For a fixed semistable source curve over the original valued field, construct the admissible correction to the determinant model metric and compare its rigidified metric with the canonical Poincaré metric. Establish compatibility with the proposed actual-form Green construction, including finite local lengths, trace normalization, and the prescribed representatives.
entries.approach: Use the smooth-model comparison as a normalization test; compute the vertical and graph corrections in semistable reduction; then verify equality with the actual-form construction on its complete test space.

entries.title: Height domination and boundaries in families
entries.summary: Connect the local theory to adelic positivity and Diophantine finiteness.
entries.statement: For families of homologically trivial cycles, identify the correct metrized biextension or height line bundle, establish its local comparison and boundary asymptotics under exact hypotheses, and determine conditions yielding height domination and Northcott on a specified open parameter locus.

references.label: Ziyang Gao and Shou-Wu Zhang — Heights of Ceresa and Gross–Schoen cycles
references.locator: 2026 version; abstract and main theorem
references.description: Lower bounds and Northcott on a Zariski-open dense moduli locus for genus at least three. The result concerns variation in a family, not positivity of every residual Chow class.

references.label: Yuta Nakayama — Asymptotics of local height pairing
references.locator: Theorem 10.9; Theorem 11.2 and Lemma 11.1
references.description: Relative biextension comparison and boundary asymptotics. The singular-fibre modification used in the cited extension has its own cohomological and Hodge-conjecture conditions.

entries.motivation: The Gross–Schoen and Ceresa families provide a geometric bridge to the broader Arakelov and Diophantine programme.
entries.approach: Start with smooth relative biextension comparison. Track the modified-cycle and cohomological hypotheses needed at singular fibres. Separate local semipositivity, geometric nefness, adelic nefness, and arithmetic height domination.

entries.title: Vanishing on the original Chow source
entries.summary: Kill the source image in a residual dual, not necessarily the entire obstruction space.
entries.motivation: An auxiliary residual quotient may be nonzero while every relevant algebraic source pairs trivially with it. The latter is the needed conclusion.
entries.approach: Identify selected periods through model boundaries or arithmetic Abel–Jacobi data; retain the original detectors and exact extension factors. Prove a source-specific annihilation or a strict finite-period estimate that forces the original periods to vanish.

entries.title: Tropical realization on the full actual test space
entries.summary: Pass from chartwise primitives to an ordinary actual form on the exact complement.
entries.statement: Develop a compatible refinement and Aeppli/Bott–Chern theory that realizes chartwise primitives as ordinary actual Mihatsch forms on the prescribed open complement, with independence of presentation, gluing, residue compatibility, and the full compact actual test identity.
entries.approach: Separate topological inverse-limit results from differential, integral, and cohomological comparison. Treat fixed finite certificates as conditional inputs until their existence for every original Chow source is established.
entries.motivation: The related Bedford–Taylor programme concerns intrinsic operations on currents and potentials. Its descent questions are useful foundations, but do not by themselves construct the required actual Green representatives.

entries.title: Numerical model curvature detection
entries.summary: A special-fibre numerical condition is proposed to detect equality of actual model Chern forms.
entries.statement:
Let \(\mathcal X\) be an integral projective flat model over the valuation ring of \(K\), with smooth projective generic fibre \(X\) of dimension \(n\). Let \(P\) be a homogeneous polynomial of degree \(r\) in the Chern classes of model bundles. The draft asserts that, if its special-fibre operational class has degree zero against every integral \(r\)-dimensional closed subvariety of \(\mathcal X_s\), then the corresponding actual model Chern form is strictly zero.

The line-bundle assertion is proved first; the proposed vector-bundle construction descends symmetric root polynomials from simultaneous flag bundles. No smoothness or reducedness of the special fibre is assumed in the source.

references.label: Andreas Mihatsch — δ-Forms on Lubin–Tate Space
references.locator: 2024 version; actual δ-forms and complete-intersection Green forms
references.description: A primary analytic framework for actual δ-forms on good Berkovich spaces. The general strong zero-curvature target in this project has additional hypotheses and conclusions.

entries.proof: Test the model curvature against products of model Hessians on a common model refinement. The operational projection formula makes each top-degree mass zero. The scalar-density detector successively replaces model-function slots by original-smooth functions using Stokes against one fixed signed measure. A local positive Hessian on a witnessing skeleton then detects a nonzero pure coefficient, giving a contradiction. For vector bundles, compare root polynomials on the double flag bundle, descend along local sections, and retain strict Whitney and Chern-character identities.
entries.approach: Audit the scalar-density induction, the witnessing-skeleton test, and the comparison between actual top wedges and native model intersection measures.

entries.title: Finite trace on scalar–curvature forms
entries.summary: The proposed trace has a specified actual-form domain and adjunction against all compact actual tests.
entries.statement:
Let \(q:Y\to X\) be finite dominant between normal integral separated \(K\)-varieties. Let \(\mathscr M^k\) be the actual scalar–curvature module locally generated by \(u_0Du_1\wedge\cdots\wedge Du_k\), with the piecewise-linear data of the source. The draft asserts a unique ordinary actual trace satisfying
\[
\int_X\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathscr M}_q(\omega)\wedge\eta
=\int_Y\omega\wedge q^*\eta
\]
for every compact complementary actual test. It is local in the ordinary topology, respects actual relations, and uses the full native generic degree.

references.label: Andreas Mihatsch — δ-Forms on Lubin–Tate Space
references.locator: 2024 version; actual δ-forms and complete-intersection Green forms
references.description: A primary analytic framework for actual δ-forms on good Berkovich spaces. The general strong zero-curvature target in this project has additional hypotheses and conclusions.

entries.proof: The pure-curvature trace is constructed by finite orbit sorting. Introduce a parameter \(t\), replace the scalar factor by the graph curvature \(D\max(u_0-t,0)\), and integrate \(\chi(t)t\) times the resulting pure-curvature trace over the parameter. The product-skeleton projection calculation and the one-parameter identity recover \(u_0\). Adjunction and injectivity of actual forms into currents are used to prove independence and uniqueness.
entries.approach: Verify actual relation descent, the product-integration domain, and the use of arbitrary compact actual tests. The trace domain remains the scalar–curvature module.

entries.title: Green pairs on the prescribed support complement
entries.summary: A supported model complex supplies the proposed curved Green identity before curvature is removed.
entries.statement:
For a specified rational codimension-\(r\) cycle \(Z\), the draft constructs an ordinary actual form \(G_Z\) on \(U_Z\) and a global separately closed actual form \(\Omega_Z\) of bidegree \((r,r)\), with
\[
\int_{U_Z}G_Z\wedge D\eta+\int_{Z^{\mathrm{an}}}\eta
=\int_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}\Omega_Z\wedge\eta
\]
for every compact actual test of bidegree \((n-r,n-r)\). The residue is the prescribed cycle with its rational coefficients, and the complement is precisely \(U_Z\).

references.label: Andreas Mihatsch — δ-Forms on Lubin–Tate Space
references.locator: 2024 version; actual δ-forms and complete-intersection Green forms
references.description: A primary analytic framework for actual δ-forms on good Berkovich spaces. The general strong zero-curvature target in this project has additional hypotheses and conclusions.

entries.proof: Resolve the components of the prescribed cycle by supported model complexes. Their localized leading characters fix the cycle coefficients. Relative line diagonalization and a smooth finite-flat multisection over the entire prescribed complement reduce the construction to PL scalar–curvature expressions. Apply the restricted trace and scalar Poincaré–Lelong, then sum the component constructions with the original coefficients.
entries.approach: Check finite flatness over the whole open complement, localized multiplicities, and convergence and adjunction for the full actual test class.

entries.title: A Chow-invariant actual Bott–Chern obstruction
entries.summary: The curvature of a model Green pair is proposed to depend only on its generic Chow class.
entries.statement:
Set
\[
H^{r,r}_{\mathrm{BC,act}}(X)=
\frac{\{\omega\in\mathcal B^{r,r}(X^{\mathrm{an}}):d'\omega=d''\omega=0\}}
{D\mathcal B^{r-1,r-1}(X^{\mathrm{an}})}.
\]
The proposed construction gives a rational-linear map
\[
\mathfrak o^r_{X,K}:\operatorname{CH}^r(X)_{\mathbf Q}
\longrightarrow H^{r,r}_{\mathrm{BC,act}}(X)
\]
represented by degree-\(r\) model Chern-character forms. It is invariant under rational equivalence and functorial for the genuine analytic pullbacks specified in (A1), including rational fibre maps.

references.label: Andreas Mihatsch — δ-Forms on Lubin–Tate Space
references.locator: 2024 version; actual δ-forms and complete-intersection Green forms
references.description: A primary analytic framework for actual δ-forms on good Berkovich spaces. The general strong zero-curvature target in this project has additional hypotheses and conclusions.

source.locator: prop:inputs (A1); see supported_green.tex, r11p:generic-k-primitive and r11p:generic-chow-primitive
source.publicationNote: Unsigned public copy; only personal attribution has been removed.

entries.proof: Generic acyclic model complexes yield global actual primitives. This handles generic \(K_0\)-relations. A rational Adams projector isolates degree \(r\), so model characters with the same generic codimension-\(r\) Chow class differ by \(D\) of a global actual form. Their classes therefore define the proposed map.
entries.motivation: The Bott–Chern target and the separately selected residual-period targets in the historical programme are different constructions. Identifying them requires the recorded comparison hypotheses.

entries.title: Removing an exact global curvature
entries.summary: A formal correction preserves the original support complement.
entries.statement:
Assume a Green pair \((G_Z,\Omega_Z)\) as in BB-SUPPORTED-GREEN-PAIR and a global actual form \(\Psi\) with \(D\Psi=\Omega_Z\). Then
\[
\gamma_Z=G_Z-\Psi|_{U_Z}
\]
satisfies the zero-curvature identity of STRONG-G on the exact same \(U_Z\). In particular, the obstruction construction and (A2) imply this conclusion whenever \(\mathfrak o^r_{X,K}([Z])=0\).

source.publicationNote: Unsigned public copy; only personal attribution has been removed.

entries.proof: Actual Stokes for the global form gives \(\int_X\Psi\wedge D\eta=\int_XD\Psi\wedge\eta=\int_X\Omega_Z\wedge\eta\). Subtract this equality from the curved Green identity. The right-hand side cancels. Since \(\Psi\) is global, its restriction removes no additional points from the domain of \(G_Z\).
entries.motivation: This is the formal implication from zero obstruction to a strong Green form. The existence of the input Green pair remains its separate analytic dependency.

entries.title: Compact additive maps into torsion-free groups
entries.summary: An elementary compactness lemma used in the algebraic-equivalence argument.
entries.statement: Let \(A\) be a compact topological abelian group and \(W\) a torsion-free abelian group. If an additive map \(\varphi:A\to W\) has kernel containing an identity neighbourhood, then \(\varphi=0\).

source.publicationNote: Unsigned public copy; only personal attribution has been removed.

entries.proof: Let \(U\subseteq\ker\varphi\) be an identity neighbourhood. Choose an open identity neighbourhood \(V\) with \(V-V\subseteq U\). Compactness gives a finite cover of \(A\) by translates of \(V\). For any \(a\in A\), two points among sufficiently many successive multiples \(0,a,2a,\ldots\) lie in the same translate. Their difference is \(ma\in U\) for some integer \(m>0\). Thus \(m\varphi(a)=\varphi(ma)=0\). Torsion-freeness implies \(\varphi(a)=0\). This holds for every \(a\).
entries.motivation: The group lemma is independent of the new actual-form constructions; the analytic work is to produce the required locally constant additive map.

entries.title: Uniform constancy along nearby rational fibres
entries.summary: The proposed actual-form rigidity supplies local constancy of the obstruction map.
entries.statement:
Let \(X/K\) be smooth and projective, let \(S/K\) be smooth and separated, and fix \(a_0\in S(K)\). For an actual form \(\omega\in\mathcal B^{p,q}((X\times_KS)^{\mathrm{an}})\), the draft asserts an ordinary neighbourhood \(V\) of \(a_0\) in \(S^{\mathrm{an}}\) such that
\[
s_a^*\omega=s_{a_0}^*\omega\qquad(a\in V\cap S(K)).
\]
The parameter is a \(K\)-rational point, and the uniform neighbourhood uses properness of \(X\).

references.label: Andreas Mihatsch — δ-Forms on Lubin–Tate Space
references.locator: 2024 version; actual δ-forms and complete-intersection Green forms
references.description: A primary analytic framework for actual δ-forms on good Berkovich spaces. The general strong zero-curvature target in this project has additional hypotheses and conclusions.

source.publicationNote: Unsigned public copy; only personal attribution has been removed.

entries.proof: Near the central fibre, write the form using a finite tuple of analytic units \(f_i\). Compare them with their pullbacks \(f_i^0\) from that fibre. Shrinking makes \(|f_i-f_i^0|<|f_i^0|\), hence their tropical moment maps agree. This gives the asserted local pullback identity. The projection to \(S^{\mathrm{an}}\) is proper and closed, so the local neighbourhoods of the compact fibre contain the full inverse image of one parameter neighbourhood.
entries.approach: Check the common domains of the local unit presentations and the claimed equality in the ordinary actual sheaf, not only equality of associated currents.

entries.title: Descent from a vertical numerical certificate
entries.summary: A certificate controls special-fibre intersections before a finite trace returns to the original field.
entries.statement:
An \(r\)-numerical certificate for \(b\in\operatorname{CH}^r(V)_{\mathbf Q}\) consists of an integral projective flat model \(\mathcal V\) and \(\xi\in K_0(\mathcal V)_{\mathbf Q}\) such that
\[
\operatorname{ch}_r(\xi|_V)=b,\qquad
\deg\bigl(\operatorname{ch}_r(\xi_s)\cap[T]\bigr)=0
\]
for every integral vertical \(r\)-dimensional closed subscheme \(T\).

Let \(h:V\to X\) be finite dominant between smooth integral projective \(K\)-varieties. The draft asserts that a certificate for \(h^*z\) implies \(\mathfrak o^r_{X,K}(z)=0\), and hence a strong Green form for each prescribed representative of \(z\). The source also allows a smooth integral variety over a finite larger constant field regarded as a \(K\)-variety, retaining its native degree and special-fibre multiplicities.

references.label: Andreas Mihatsch — δ-Forms on Lubin–Tate Space
references.locator: 2024 version; actual δ-forms and complete-intersection Green forms
references.description: A primary analytic framework for actual δ-forms on good Berkovich spaces. The general strong zero-curvature target in this project has additional hypotheses and conclusions.

entries.proof: Pass to the closure of the generic graph so that the certificate and the pulled-back model character live on a common model. Model refinements preserve the certificate by operational projection. The numerical detector makes the certificate curvature strictly zero, and generic Chow invariance supplies a structured global primitive upstairs. Apply the restricted trace to the original scalar–curvature generators along their composite finite maps, divide by the full native degree, and test against all compact actual forms. This produces the proposed global primitive downstairs. Finally apply BB-GREEN-CORRECTION.
entries.motivation: The composite-trace construction uses the original generators; it does not require a previously traced form to belong again to the trace module.

entries.title: The semistable abelian numerical stage
entries.summary: Vertical correction on a Künnemann model supplies the certificate needed by finite numerical descent.
entries.statement: Assume the local semistable model theorem stated as thm:kunnemann-local in the source and the analytic conclusions of BB-FINITE-NUMERICAL-DESCENT. For an abelian variety \(A/K\), every geometrically homologically trivial rational class of codimension \(1\le r\le\dim A\) has zero actual obstruction. Each prescribed representative then has a strong Green form over the original valued field.
entries.proof: After finite extension choose the regular projective semistable abelian model. Extend the generic class to a Chow class \(\Theta\). Its component restrictions give a class \(a\) in the special-fibre component complex. Geometric homological triviality and the cited cycle-class injectivity give \(a\cap[Y]=0\). Exactness supplies a vertical class \(\beta\) with \(i^*i_*\beta=a\). Replacing \(\Theta\) by \(\Theta-i_*\beta\) makes every component restriction homologically trivial. Its pure virtual model-bundle representative is a numerical certificate. Apply finite numerical descent.
entries.motivation: Künnemann already constructed classical height pairings on abelian varieties. This stage concerns the proposed stronger actual-form realization and its support and test conditions.

entries.title: The Chow diagonal of a pointed product
entries.summary: A purely algebraic factorization through one abelian variety, with degree shifts.
entries.statement:
Let \(F\) have characteristic zero. Let \(A/F\) be abelian and \(C_1,\ldots,C_s\) smooth projective geometrically integral curves with \(F\)-rational points. Put
\[
X=A\times_F\prod_i C_i,\qquad B=A\times_F\prod_i\operatorname{Jac}(C_i).
\]
There are finitely many rational Chow correspondences \(u_j:X\rightsquigarrow B\) and \(v_j:B\rightsquigarrow X\) of opposite degree shifts with
\[
\sum_jv_j\circ u_j=\Delta_X
\quad\text{in }\operatorname{CH}^{\dim X}(X\times_FX)_{\mathbf Q}.
\]
entries.proof: The pointed curve projectors split \(h(C_i)=\mathbf1\oplus h^1(C_i)\oplus\mathbb L\). The Abel–Jacobi and Poincaré correspondences identify \(h^1(C_i)\) with the degree-one summand of its Jacobian motive. Tensor these splittings and the identity on \(A\). Each summand factors through \(A\) times a subproduct of the Jacobians, with a Tate twist. Projection from \(B\) to that subproduct has a zero-section, giving a Chow retraction. Sum the finitely many inclusions and retractions to obtain the diagonal.
entries.motivation: This Chow identity is an algebraic ingredient. Its validity neither supplies regular models nor proves the analytic correspondence-transfer interface.

entries.title: Simultaneous regular models for the product route
entries.summary: The geometric reduction needs regular models as well as a Chow diagonal.
entries.statement: For an abelian variety \(A/K\) and smooth projective geometrically integral curves \(C_i/K\), the draft asserts one finite extension \(F/K\) over which the curves have rational points and regular projective strictly semistable models; the product \(A_F\times\prod_i C_{i,F}\) has a regular projective strictly semistable model; and \(B=A_F\times\prod_i\operatorname{Jac}(C_{i,F})\) has a regular projective semistable model satisfying the cited Künnemann component theorem.
entries.proof: Choose a finite extension giving rational points and semistable models for the curves, then enlarge it for the abelian model and the required model of \(B\). Regularize earlier models after ramified base change by the cited sequence of blowups. Apply the cited product regularization repeatedly. The blowups preserve projectivity and the prescribed smooth generic fibres.
entries.approach: Check the exact hypotheses of the semistable abelian model theorem and the base-change and product regularization references for one common final field.

entries.title: Chow transfer with the regular-model hypotheses
entries.summary: The expanded draft has a more explicit model-sensitive transfer criterion.
entries.statement:
Assume the numerical detector, finite numerical descent, and supported numerical correspondence-transfer statements of the standalone draft. Suppose that after a finite extension \(F/K\): (i) \(X_F\) has a regular integral projective flat model; (ii) an abelian variety \(B/F\) has the regular projective semistable model satisfying thm:kunnemann-local; and (iii) finitely many rational Chow correspondences with opposite degree shifts satisfy
\[
\sum_j v_j\circ u_j=\Delta_{X_F}.
\]
Then each prescribed geometrically homologically trivial rational cycle on \(X\) has a strong Green form over the original \(K\).
entries.proof: Each \((u_j)_*z_F\) is homologically trivial on \(B\), so the abelian model supplies a numerical certificate. The supported numerical projection argument transfers each certificate along \(v_j\) to the chosen regular model of \(X_F\). Summing gives a certificate for \(z_F\) by the actual Chow diagonal identity. Finite numerical descent for \(X_F\to X\) returns the Green construction with its full factor \([F:K]\).
entries.approach: Independently audit the supported numerical projection and alteration argument in prop:correspondence-transfer. The regular target model is an explicit hypothesis of this version.

entries.title: H16 on its fixed global kernel domain
entries.summary: The recovered assembly proof constructs a pairing on admitted kernels; the fixed finite-detector presentation requires its separate witness comparison.
entries.statement:
Assume the frozen H16 assembly hypotheses and the fixed FD17 global-witness conditions recorded in the source synthesis. For a number-field variety \(X/F\), with \(S\) and its detectors fixed before the cycle, set
\[
\mathcal H^r(X)=\ker\left(
\operatorname{CH}^r(X)_{\mathbf Q,\mathrm{geom\,hom}}
\xrightarrow{P_X^r}\bigoplus_{w\in S}V_{w,r}^{\vee}\right).
\]
The source records a normalized real-valued analytic Beilinson–Bloch pairing on these kernel domains in complementary codimensions. Both factors must lie in their respective domains. Passing to the complete homologically trivial Chow groups requires vanishing of the detector periods of localized global classes in both codimensions.

source.locator: r16h:height-domain; r16h:global-height. The finite FD17 presentation additionally uses the fixed-witness comparison recorded in editions 0.1.0–0.2.0.

entries.proof: The complete H16 argument constructs normalized local values, proves reciprocity and independence of the chosen Green form, establishes finite support of the global sum, and descends through rational equivalence on the intersection of the local obstruction kernels at all finite completions. The new global height paper retains this proof under its explicit analytic hypotheses. Identifying this all-completion domain with the finite-detector kernel displayed above requires the additional fixed FD17 witness comparison; good-place vanishing alone does not furnish that comparison. HA16 and MM16 supply adjunction and model comparison under their separate hypotheses.
entries.motivation: The fixed global-source target may be weaker than strong G for every local Chow class. It gives a distinct intermediate route to the global height problem without asserting positivity or nondegeneracy.
