introduction.title: Results on Beilinson–Bloch height pairings
introduction.summary: The main construction is a real-valued bilinear pairing on Chow classes whose local Bott–Chern obstructions vanish. The geometric results identify classes for which this vanishing holds, including several families where both entire homologically trivial Chow groups are covered. The standing analytic hypotheses—Green forms, obstruction covariance and local reciprocity—remain under independent review; additional model hypotheses are stated case by case.
introduction.convention: Let \(X/F\) be a smooth projective geometrically integral variety of dimension \(n\) over a number field. Write \(V^r(X)=\operatorname{CH}^r(X)_{\mathbf Q,\mathrm{hom}}\) for geometrically homologically trivial rational Chow classes, and set \[\mathcal H^r(X)=\{z\in V^r(X):\mathfrak o^r_{X_{F_v}}(z_{F_v})=0\text{ for every finite place }v\},\] where \(\mathfrak o^r_{X_{F_v}}\) is the local Bott–Chern obstruction. The pairing is \(h_X:\mathcal H^r(X)\times\mathcal H^s(X)\to\mathbf R\), where \(r+s=n+1\). To obtain it on \(V^r(X)\times V^s(X)\), the local vanishing must hold in both degrees.
introduction.evidence: The geometric arguments are proved under explicit hypotheses on Green forms, the Bott–Chern obstruction and its functoriality, and local reciprocity. Their companion analytic proofs are available but have not completed independent mathematical review. Additional model or comparison hypotheses are specified in each case; the linked papers give the full statements and proofs.

groups.title: 1. Pairings on cycle groups
groups.summary: The general construction first gives a pairing on the common kernel of the local obstruction maps. Algebraic equivalence and the divisor, zero-cycle and one-cycle calculations then identify subgroups on which it is defined.

cases.title: A height pairing when the local obstruction vanishes
cases.result: Under the Green-form and reciprocity hypotheses, the sum of local Green integrals is independent of representatives and Green forms. It defines a rational-bilinear pairing, symmetric in the complementary factors and invariant under finite extension of the number field.
cases.established: At each finite place, subtract a global primitive from a Green form to remove its curvature. The residue identity gives the local transformation law under rational equivalence. Almost all local terms vanish, and the number-field product formula makes their weighted sum descend to Chow classes. The archimedean terms use the classical complex Green construction.

additionalProofs.label: Proof of the global pairing and reciprocity

dependencies: The supported Green-form construction and the local point-residue identity
Stokes, finite trace, good-reduction vanishing and the principal transformation law
Correspondence adjunction and arithmetic-model comparison for the additional formulas below
cases.gap: For a general variety, the unresolved extension is to prove that every localized global homologically trivial class has zero obstruction in each complementary degree. The finite-period description of this kernel additionally requires the specified comparison theorem.

cases.title: Height pairings on algebraically trivial cycles
cases.result: In every dimension and codimension, the algebraically trivial subgroup is contained in the kernel of every local obstruction. Thus either algebraically trivial factor can be paired with the complementary group on which the general construction is defined.
cases.domain: \[\operatorname{CH}^r(X)_{\mathbf Q,\mathrm{alg}}\times\mathcal H^{n+1-r}(X)\longrightarrow\mathbf R.\] In particular both factors may be algebraically trivial. Algebraic equivalence is taken over an algebraic closure.
cases.established: Express an algebraically trivial cycle through a family parametrized by a smooth projective curve. The Poincaré bundle makes the obstruction an additive, locally constant map from a compact p-adic abelian group to a real vector space. Its image is finite and torsion-free, hence zero. Alternatively, transfer the vanishing for degree-zero divisors on the parameter curve by its Chow correspondence. Descent along the finite field extension returns the result to the original field.

additionalProofs.label: Alternative proof using compact parameter spaces

dependencies: Chow invariance of the obstruction and Green forms on the prescribed support complement
Local constancy along rational parameter fibers, or the divisor theorem and functoriality under Chow correspondences
The global pairing on the common local kernel
cases.gap: To replace the second factor by its entire homologically trivial Chow group, one must establish local obstruction vanishing in that complementary degree.

cases.title: Divisors, zero-cycles and one-cycles
cases.result: The local obstruction vanishes on homologically trivial divisors, zero-cycles and one-cycles. Consequently the divisor–zero-cycle pairing has both full factors on every variety; in dimension three this also gives the complete middle pairing.
cases.domain: \[h_X:V^1(X)\times V^n(X)\to\mathbf R.\] For \(n\ge2\), one also obtains \(V^{n-1}(X)\times\mathcal H^2(X)\to\mathbf R\).
cases.established: For one-cycles, pull the class to a strictly semistable alteration, correct its extension on the regular model to have zero vertical intersection numbers, and descend the obstruction vanishing. Together with the divisor and zero-cycle results, this covers every codimension in dimensions at most three.

proof.label: Proofs for divisors, zero-cycles and one-cycles

dependencies: The divisor and zero-cycle results and the regular-model correction for one-cycles
Detection of the obstruction after a dominant map, with the full field and generic degrees
The global pairing on the common local kernel
cases.gap: In higher dimensions, the one-cycle result leaves the codimension-two factor to be determined. The regular-model correction and descent are explicit analytic inputs to this deduction.

children.title: Varieties of dimension at most three
children.text: Every complementary pair is covered. In particular, for every smooth projective threefold the construction gives \(h_X:V^2(X)\times V^2(X)\to\mathbf R\), under the same analytic hypotheses.

cases.title: A period criterion for individual cycle classes
cases.result: A class belongs to the pairing domain if its specified local obstruction periods vanish at every relevant bad place. This criterion can be applied to individual classes and their rational linear combinations.
cases.domain: Classes \(z\in V^r(X)\) and \(w\in V^{n+1-r}(X)\) satisfying the period criterion in their respective degrees.
cases.established: Fix the comparison identifying the local obstruction with finitely many rational intersection periods. Their vanishing places the class in the local kernel. Good reduction handles the remaining places, and the Green-form construction supplies a representative on the original support complement.

proof.label: The period criterion and Green forms

dependencies: The stated finite-period comparison, chosen before the cycle classes
Reconstruction in the original form sheaf and against every actual test
Good-reduction compatibility and the global pairing
cases.gap: The open problem is to prove these original periods vanish for every homologically trivial class. A finite list of periods alone does not establish that vanishing.

children.title: Differences of complete intersections
children.text: For the specified comparison matrices between regular section tuples, the tropical construction extends their Green-form difference across canceled components. The resulting form is defined on the exact support complement of the difference cycle. Such differences are rationally equivalent to zero, so their global height against every allowed complementary class is zero.

groups.title: 2. Chow decompositions and geometric applications
groups.summary: If a rational Chow decomposition expresses a cycle as a sum of correspondence images of classes with vanishing obstruction, the obstruction of the original cycle vanishes. Applying this in both complementary degrees gives pairings on the entire homologically trivial groups.

cases.title: Varieties with a Chow motive of abelian type
cases.result: Both homologically trivial Chow groups are covered in every complementary pair of codimensions when, after finite extension, the diagonal factors through abelian varieties in rational Chow motives.
cases.domain: \[h_X:V^r(X)\times V^{n+1-r}(X)\to\mathbf R,\qquad 1\le r\le n,\] provided \(\Delta_{X_E}=\sum_jv_j\circ u_j\) in rational Chow, with \(u_j,v_j\) factoring through abelian varieties and having opposite degree shifts.
cases.established: Künnemann’s semistable model theorem gives a vertical correction of a homologically trivial cycle on an abelian variety. The numerical comparison then gives zero obstruction. Apply the Chow correspondences term by term to the diagonal identity and descend by the full field degree. A decomposition acting as the identity in one degree suffices for that degree.

proof.label: Proof by Chow correspondences from abelian varieties

additionalProofs.label: Local proof of numerical correction and descent

dependencies: The comparison between numerical model intersections and the Bott–Chern obstruction
Functoriality under Chow correspondences and finite descent; the global pairing theorem
cases.gap: The factorization must hold in rational Chow groups. A decomposition only in cohomology or modulo numerical equivalence does not supply the required identity.

children.title: Correspondence images of abelian varieties
children.text: Every rational sum of images of homologically trivial abelian classes has vanishing obstruction. A diagonal decomposition is needed to conclude this for every class of the target, but not for an individual correspondence image.

children.title: Products of curves and abelian varieties
children.text: The Chow projectors of a pointed curve factor through its Jacobian. Tensoring these identities gives the result for finite products, after choosing the points over a finite extension.

children.title: Separated-variable hypersurfaces
children.text: For sums of reduced binary forms and nonzero pure powers, the Shioda–Katsura construction, the blowup formula and a generically finite degree retraction give the required Chow decomposition. Fermat and diagonal hypersurfaces are included.

children.title: Separated-variable cubic hypersurfaces
children.text: Laterveer’s theorem supplies a Chow motive of abelian type for the specified cubic blocks. Descending the finite correspondence and rational-equivalence data gives, in particular, the cubic tenfold and twelvefold families stated in the paper.

children.title: Cyclic covers with separated branch equations
children.text: A finite flat map from a separated-variable hypersurface gives a Chow retraction. Its rank and the degree of the number field contribute separately to the normalized height formula.

children.title: Finite products and forms over finite extensions
children.text: Tensoring the diagonal decompositions treats products. Transporting them through an isomorphism over a finite extension, followed by degree descent, treats the corresponding forms.

cases.title: Products of curves and surfaces
cases.result: Subject to the product-model theorem, the construction covers every complementary pair of homologically trivial Chow groups on a product of arbitrary curves and surfaces, and on the stated Chow-motive summands of such products.
cases.domain: \(V^r(X)\times V^{n+1-r}(X)\), where \(X=T\times\prod_a C_a\times\prod_b S_b\), the \(C_a\) are smooth projective curves, the \(S_b\) are smooth projective surfaces, and \(T\) has potentially good projective reduction at every finite place. One may take \(T\) to be a point.
cases.status: Conditional theorem with an additional model hypothesis
cases.established: On a semistable resolution of the product, the model theorem constructs an algebraic generalized inverse to the restriction–Gysin operator on full cohomology. This supplies the algebraic corrections required by the numerical criterion. Weight–monodromy for curves and surfaces and finite descent then give local obstruction vanishing. The same argument applies to new cycle classes after any finite extension.

proof.label: Proof for products of curves and surfaces

dependencies: The algebraic generalized inverse on the specified semistable product model
The comparison of the restriction–Gysin operator, numerical intersections and the local obstruction
Weight–monodromy, dominant descent and the global pairing theorem
cases.gap: The additional step is the product-model calculation on full cohomology, including its transcendental summands and exceptional components. This argument does not reduce an arbitrary surface motive to an abelian-type motive.

children.title: Chow motives generated by curves and surfaces
children.text: The result passes to direct summands of finite sums of Tate-twisted motives of these products. Arbitrary abelian factors are allowed, because an abelian variety is a rational Chow-motive summand of a product of curves after finite extension.

children.title: Hilbert schemes of points on surfaces
children.text: The de Cataldo–Migliorini incidence decomposition expresses the motive through powers of the surface. This also treats finite products with curves and the permitted potentially good reduction factor.

children.title: Moduli spaces on K3 and abelian surfaces
children.text: For the smooth projective moduli spaces covered by Bülles’s theorem, the rational Chow motive is a summand of motives of powers of the underlying surface. Specialization of the finite correspondence identities to a number field gives the asserted pairing domain.

cases.title: Varieties with a decomposition of the diagonal
cases.result: A diagonal supported on a divisor in one term and on a subvariety of dimension at most three in the other gives the entire pairing in dimensions at most five, and the indicated outer complementary degrees in higher dimensions.
cases.domain: Assume \(\Delta_X=A+B\) in rational Chow, with \(\operatorname{Supp}A\subset D\times X\), \(D\) a divisor, and \(\operatorname{Supp}B\subset X\times T\), \(\dim T\le3\). Then \(h_X\) is defined on \(V^r(X)\times V^{n+1-r}(X)\) for every \(r\) if \(n\le5\), and for \(r\le2\) or \(r\ge n-1\) otherwise.
cases.established: The diagonal and its transpose send the relevant classes to divisors, zero-cycles or one-cycles on resolutions of the supports. The local vanishing holds for \(r\le2\) or \(r\ge n-2\). Intersect this range with the range for \(n+1-r\) to obtain the stated global pairings.

proof.label: Proof using the decomposition of the diagonal

dependencies: Vanishing for divisors, zero-cycles and one-cycles
Functoriality under rational Chow correspondences and finite descent
Local vanishing at every finite place in both complementary degrees
cases.gap: The diagonal identity, or a hypothesis proving universal support of zero-cycles, is essential. In higher dimensions the middle complementary degrees remain outside this deduction.

children.title: Universal support of zero-cycles
children.text: If zero-cycles are universally supported on a subvariety of dimension at most three, the generic-point rational equivalence spreads to the required diagonal after a finite extension.

children.title: Rationally connected fibrations and Fano varieties
children.text: A multisection of a rationally connected fibration over a base of dimension at most three gives universal support of zero-cycles. In particular the theorem applies to geometrically rationally connected varieties, including smooth Fano varieties, with the stated dimension and degree ranges.

children.title: Geometrically unirational varieties of dimension at most five
children.text: The whole pairing is obtained in every complementary degree. In dimension five this includes the middle pairing \(V^3(X)\times V^3(X)\to\mathbf R\).

children.title: Geometrically uniruled fourfolds
children.text: Resolving a rational domination by a threefold times \(\mathbf P^1\) introduces only centers of dimension at most two. The blowup formula and dominant descent give both \(V^2(X)\times V^3(X)\) and the divisor–zero-cycle pair.

children.title: Projective bundles, blowups and dominant morphisms
children.text: The property passes to projective bundles, to blowups when the ambient variety and center are already covered, and to smooth projective dominant morphism images. Thus projective-bundle towers over varieties of dimension at most three or over the preceding uniruled fourfolds, and their dominant morphism images, have every complementary pairing. Replacing such a morphism by a rational map requires control of its resolution centers.

cases.title: Chow niveau, complete intersections and fibrations
cases.result: If the part of the Chow motive not accounted for by abelian varieties is supported in sufficiently small dimension, the divisor and one-cycle results give additional full complementary pairings. Known Chow decompositions apply this criterion to the complete intersections and fibrations listed below.
cases.domain: Suppose \(h(X)=Q\oplus(T,e,u)\), where \(Q\) is of abelian type, \(u\ge0\), and \(\dim T\le n-2u\). The pairing on \(V^r(X)\times V^{n+1-r}(X)\) exists for every \(r\) if \(n\le2u+3\), and otherwise for \(r\le u+1\) or \(r\ge n-u\).
cases.established: The residual summand sends the relevant cycles to divisors or one-cycles on \(T\), giving local vanishing for \(r\le u+1\) or \(r\ge n-u-1\). Vial’s Chow decompositions and the cited low-degree Chow-group bounds supply the required factorizations. For intersections of quadrics, a self-intersection calculation gives the signed Chow retraction.

proof.label: Proofs using Chow niveau and fibration theorems

dependencies: Vial’s rational Chow-motive decompositions with their stated hypotheses
Vanishing on abelian varieties and in the divisor, zero-cycle and one-cycle degrees
The cited low-degree Chow-group theorems and the global pairing theorem
cases.gap: The fibration criterion requires the Chow-group condition on every geometric scheme fiber, including singular fibers. Outside the displayed ranges, the residual motive may contain degrees not covered by the divisor and one-cycle calculations.

children.title: Small-degree complete intersections
children.text: Every complementary pairing is obtained for cubics of dimensions 6, 7, 8, 9 and 11; quartics of dimension 7; intersections of type (2,3) of dimensions 6, 7 and 9; and types (2,2,3) and (3,3) of dimension 7. Cubics of dimension at most five follow from the preceding diagonal theorem.

children.title: Quadric and cubic fibrations
children.text: For the flat projective fibrations in the theorem, all pairings are obtained for quadric fibers over bases of dimensions 1–3, and for odd-dimensional quadric fibers over a four-dimensional base whose local obstructions vanish. The stated cubic fiber/base dimensions are (5,1), (5,2), (6,1) and (8,1).

children.title: Intersections of quadrics
children.text: A smooth intersection of \(c\) quadrics in \(\mathbf P^N\) has every complementary pairing when \(c\le4\), or when \(c=5\) and \(N\) is even. For other values the paper gives explicit outer-degree ranges.

children.title: Relative intersections of quadrics
children.text: Under the regular-section, flatness and expected-codimension hypotheses, all pairings are obtained when \(b+c\le5\) for even \(N\), or \(b+c\le4\) for odd \(N\). Here \(b\) is the base dimension, \(c\) the number of quadrics, and the local obstruction must vanish on the base in every degree.

groups.title: 3. Model criteria and arithmetic families
groups.summary: A cycle extension with zero intersection against the relevant vertical cycles has vanishing local obstruction, under the numerical comparison. Applying the criterion at every finite place in both complementary degrees gives a global height pairing.

cases.title: Numerical corrections on regular models
cases.result: A numerically trivial extension on a regular model is a sufficient condition for a cycle to belong to the local obstruction kernel. The criteria below produce such extensions by intersection theory on the special fiber.
cases.domain: At each finite place, require a pure operational representative on the stated dominant model with zero degree against every vertical test cycle. If every class in both \(V^r(X)\) and \(V^{n+1-r}(X)\) has such a representative, the pairing is defined on their full product. For individual classes satisfying the criterion, the conclusion is a pairing on the corresponding subgroups.
cases.established: Extend the pulled-back cycle to a regular model and modify it by a vertical class. If the corrected extension has zero intersection with every vertical test cycle, the model comparison annihilates its Bott–Chern obstruction. Descent along the dominant map and the finite field extension then gives vanishing on the original variety.
dependencies: Comparison between vertical intersection numbers and the Bott–Chern obstruction
The stated specialization and primitive-residual identities on the model
Dominant descent with all multiplicities and field degrees retained
cases.gap: The required vertical correction is established only under the listed model hypotheses. Constructing it for arbitrary models and arbitrary homologically trivial cycles remains the general problem.

children.title: One-dimensional Gysin images
children.text: When the sum of the Gysin images is one-dimensional on each component, the correction reduces to a weighted graph Laplacian. The dual graph is required to be connected, with the intersection and residue degrees used as weights.

children.title: Positive primitive intersection forms on fourfolds
children.text: The primitive-residual identity is a weighted sum of nonnegative self-intersections. Positive definiteness forces every residual to vanish, giving codimension two; the divisor, zero-cycle and one-cycle cases supply the other degrees.

children.title: Multiplicity-free finite-group actions
children.text: If the rational primitive representation is multiplicity-free and its intersection form is nondegenerate, an invariant totally isotropic residual must be zero. Restricting this argument to suitable isotypic components gives a subgroup that pairs with the complementary local kernel.

cases.title: Good reduction and semistable reduction
cases.result: The stated good-reduction, ordinary-quadratic and semistable-model criteria give vanishing of every local obstruction. If a criterion applies at every finite place, the global construction covers every complementary pair of homologically trivial Chow groups.
cases.domain: \(h_X:V^r(X)\times V^{n+1-r}(X)\to\mathbf R\) for all \(r\), provided the corresponding all-degree reduction criterion is satisfied at every finite place. The finite extensions and newly defined classes allowed by each theorem are retained.
cases.established: Ordinary quadratic singularities are resolved to models whose new components and intersections are quadrics with controlled intersection maps. For the semistable criteria, algebraic correspondences on the strata supply the corrections; weight–monodromy or the stated total-degeneration assumptions eliminate the remaining periods.

proof.label: Proofs for ordinary quadratic and semistable models

dependencies: The ordinary quadratic normal forms and resolution theorem, including residue characteristic two
Compatibility of semistable modification and the restriction–Gysin maps after ramified extension
The stated weight–monodromy or totally degenerate stratum hypotheses and the period comparison
cases.gap: The generalization requires the same algebraic control of restriction and Gysin maps for arbitrary singular fibers. The companion model and period-comparison results are additional inputs, not consequences of the global summation argument.

children.title: Ordinary quadratic singularities
children.text: In dimension at least three, assume an integral flat projective model has integral geometric special fiber, smooth except for finitely many points with smooth quadric projectivized tangent cones. The criterion includes residue characteristic two, the stated dominant-model variant, and new cycle classes after finite extension.

children.title: Semistable models with abelian-type strata
children.text: Every connected closed geometric stratum of the supplied regular projective reduced strictly semistable model must have a rational Chow motive of abelian type, and the specified weight–monodromy assertion must hold. A potentially good projective factor is also allowed.

children.title: Drinfeld uniformization
children.text: For the specified smooth projective algebraizations of compact torsion-free Drinfeld quotients, the strata have Tate motives and Ito’s weight–monodromy theorem applies. Products and the permitted potentially good projective factor are included.

children.title: Totally degenerate reduction
children.text: Finite generation of the integral Chow groups of the strata, positivity on primitive classes, and the stated integral cycle-class isomorphisms give the required period vanishing. Smooth projective toric strata satisfy these conditions.

cases.title: Arithmetic families from Lefschetz pencils
cases.result: The local model criteria yield Zariski-dense sets of varieties for which every complementary height pairing is defined, under the same analytic hypotheses. The density is in the particular coefficient or section space stated in each theorem.
cases.domain: For every constructed member, \(V^r(X_E)\times V^{n+1-r}(X_E)\to\mathbf R\) for all \(r\) and every finite extension \(E\) of the fixed number field in the corresponding theorem.
cases.established: Choose congruences that preserve the required local smoothings and good reduction at exceptional primes. A Lefschetz pencil with one fixed smooth member gives ordinary quadratic reduction elsewhere. The local vanishing criteria then apply at every completion, and their finite-extension versions treat newly defined cycle classes.

proof.label: Construction by Lefschetz pencils and congruences

dependencies: The prescribed free module of sections and surjectivity to the required residue spaces
A nonempty open set of Lefschetz pencils through the chosen smooth member
The local smoothing and reduction theorems, including new cycles after finite extension
cases.gap: The construction establishes density in the stated parameter spaces. It does not establish the local hypotheses for every member; where embedding polynomials are used, density in the full linear system additionally requires that they span its sections.

children.title: Hypersurfaces and complete intersections
children.text: The construction gives dense degree-D hypersurface families of dimension n for n≥3 and D≥3. It also gives successive sections of degree at least three on the specified relative complete-intersection models, over one fixed finite extension.

children.title: Divisors in products with projective space
children.text: The examples include the stated bidegree systems on projective products, systems on a surface times projective space, and systems on a fourfold times a projective line. The cohomological signature, good-reduction and section-spanning assumptions remain those of the corresponding theorem.

children.title: Products of elliptic curves and projective spaces
children.text: Four explicit families occur on \(E^2\times\mathbf P^3\) and \(E^4\times\mathbf P^1\), for the everywhere-good elliptic curve over the specified field. They have distinct monodromy ranks, and each is obtained from the same local-model and congruence-pencil method.

groups.title: 4. Comparison and arithmetic properties
groups.summary: Comparison identifies the constructed pairing with established height pairings or arithmetic intersection numbers on their common domains. Positivity, nondegeneracy and finiteness are additional questions about a pairing that has already been defined.

cases.title: Comparison with classical height pairings
cases.result: Under the correspondence and model comparison theorems, the analytic pairing is a sum of classical abelian height pairings, or the normalized arithmetic intersection of numerically admissible lifts. The resulting formulas are independent of the chosen factorization or lifts.
cases.domain: Pairs in \(\mathcal H^r(X)\times\mathcal H^{n+1-r}(X)\) with the stated abelian Chow factorization or regular numerically admissible arithmetic lifts.
cases.established: For a factorization through abelian varieties over \(E\), correspondence adjunction gives \[h_X(z,w)=\frac{1}{[E:\mathbf Q]}\sum_j\langle u_{j*}z_E,{}^tv_{j*}w_E\rangle_{A_j,\mathrm{Kun}}.\] For admissible lifts on a regular arithmetic model over \(F\), the corresponding formula is \(h_X(z,w)=[F:\mathbf Q]^{-1}\widehat{\deg}(\widehat\Theta\cdot\widehat\Phi)\). A degree-\(d\) alteration over \(E\) contributes the factor \(1/(d[E:\mathbf Q])\).

proof.label: Proofs of the height comparison formulas

dependencies: The global pairing and its invariance under finite number-field extension
Comparison with Künnemann’s abelian heights and with regular arithmetic models
cases.gap: Agreement of the analytic, arithmetic-model and determinant constructions requires the stated comparison. For arbitrary bad reduction, the missing part is the corresponding admissible metric and its comparison identity.

children.title: Blowups and Shioda–Katsura constructions
children.text: The codimension-two blowup formula subtracts the height on the center, with the sign determined by the exceptional normal bundle. A finite flat cover contributes the inverse of its full rank, separately from the number-field normalization.

children.title: Determinant metrics and Deligne pairings
children.text: The determinant paper proves the stated comparison identities at complex places and for smooth models. Extending them to the required admissible metrics at general bad-reduction places is an open problem.

cases.title: Arithmetic hard Lefschetz, positivity and finiteness
cases.result: For products of pointed curves with a height satisfying the stated axioms, Chow projectors reduce arithmetic hard Lefschetz and positivity to specified middle-degree groups. Integral height finiteness further requires arithmetic control of the integral image and its fields of definition.
cases.domain: Products of pointed curves and the residual quotient groups defined in the arithmetic-reductions paper, with a supplied height system satisfying its four axioms.
cases.established: Tensor Chow projectors isolate the middle-degree summands. An orthogonal decomposition separates a Néron–Tate part from a residual pairing on a Griffiths quotient. The Abel–Jacobi kernel controls the degeneracy question; lattice and field-of-definition criteria supply the additional conditions for a Northcott theorem.

proof.label: Proofs of the Lefschetz and Northcott reductions

dependencies: A height with bilinearity, symmetry, absolute field invariance, correspondence adjunction and the stated curve normalization
The specified Chow projectors and integral images of cycle classes
cases.gap: The remaining assertions concern the residual height, its real positivity and integral discreteness, and the fields of definition of bounded-height classes. Positivity on a rational vector space alone does not give the Northcott property.

overview.title: From Green forms to height pairings
overview.summary: The first aim is to construct Beilinson–Bloch height pairings from local Green forms. The further aims are to identify these pairings with classical constructions, prove positivity, and establish finiteness for integral classes. Each passage has its own hypotheses.
overview.target:
For a smooth, projective and geometrically integral variety \(X/F\) of dimension \(n\) over a number field, construct a canonical pairing
\[
h_X:\operatorname{CH}^r(X)_{\mathbb Q,\mathrm{hom}}\times\operatorname{CH}^{n+1-r}(X)_{\mathbb Q,\mathrm{hom}}\longrightarrow\mathbb R.
\]

implications.assumptions: A Green pair on the prescribed complement and a global actual primitive of its curvature.
implications.conclusion: A zero-curvature Green form for that prescribed cycle, against all actual tests.
implications.label: Curvature correction

implications.assumptions: The height construction on the intersection of the local obstruction kernels, and vanishing for global classes in both complementary degrees.
implications.conclusion: The same pairing is defined on both full homologically trivial Chow groups.
implications.label: Enlargement of the domain

implications.assumptions: Strong G in both degrees, together with the hypotheses on proper intersections, principal divisors, reciprocity and good reduction in the direct construction.
implications.conclusion: A symmetric Chow pairing with the stated base-extension and biextension properties. Correspondence adjunction and classical comparison have separate proofs.
implications.label: Direct construction of the pairing

problems.title: Green forms and finite trace
problems.goal: Construct a Green pair for every prescribed cycle over the original non-Archimedean field.
problems.method: Prove the supported construction and its trace identities on the actual form space. Trace must preserve differential relations and adjunction against every compact actual test, with the full field-degree normalization.
problems.output: Once the curvature has a global actual primitive, subtracting it gives Strong G on the same support complement.
problems.depends: The actual differential calculus and the supported Chern-form construction.

problems.title: Vanishing of the Bott–Chern class
problems.goal: Show that homologically trivial cycles have zero curvature class in the actual Bott–Chern quotient.
problems.method: First apply the algebraic-equivalence and Chow-correspondence arguments on their stated domains. For the remaining classes, seek a comparison theorem showing that vanishing of the cohomological cycle class forces every actual obstruction period to vanish.
problems.output: Together with Step 1, this is a sufficient route to Strong G. The tropical approach is an alternative method for constructing the required actual primitives, with its own descent and integration comparisons.
problems.depends: Step 1 for the passage from obstruction vanishing to a Green form.

problems.title: Construction of the global height pairing
problems.goal: Establish a local sum which is independent of Green representatives and descends through rational equivalence in both variables.
problems.method: Use the existing construction on the intersection of the obstruction kernels at all finite completions, then prove vanishing on localizations of global classes in both degrees. Alternatively, use directly supplied strong Green forms with proper-intersection formulas, compatibility with principal divisors under pushforward, reciprocity and vanishing at good places.
problems.output: A symmetric pairing on the desired Chow groups, with the specified field normalization. A finite-detector description requires its own comparison theorem.
problems.depends: The local calculus and global reciprocity. The second route assumes Strong G directly and need not prove vanishing of the chosen obstruction map.

problems.title: Correspondence adjunction and classical heights
problems.goal: Prove that the constructed pairing has the required correspondence identity and agrees with the classical height on common domains.
problems.method: Apply the proper-intersection projection formula to correspondences. Compare the finite-place terms on supplied admissible arithmetic models, and match the archimedean determinant and Poincaré normalizations. At bad reduction, construct the required vertical corrections.
problems.output: Identification with the classical Beilinson–Bloch pairing on the common domain, together with the normalization needed for subsequent height identities.
problems.depends: Step 3 and the additional projection-formula and admissible-model hypotheses used by each comparison.

problems.title: Arithmetic Lefschetz and positivity
problems.goal: For pointed products of curves, prove the Chow vanishing and central positivity assertions used by the arithmetic reduction theorem.
problems.formula: \(\Pi_*\operatorname{CH}^c(Y)_{\mathbb Q,\mathrm{hom}}=0\quad(k\ne2c-1),\qquad Y=\prod_{i=1}^{k}C_i\), where \(\Pi=\bigotimes_i(\Delta_{C_i}-o_i\times C_i-C_i\times o_i)\) is the projector onto the product of the \(h^1(C_i)\) factors.
problems.method: Work separately on off-central vanishing, injectivity of the central algebraic Abel–Jacobi map, and real positive definiteness of the residual height. Keep the fixed product polarization and the height axioms H1–H4 throughout.
problems.output: Under H1–H4, these assertions yield arithmetic hard Lefschetz, primitive positivity and complementary nondegeneracy by the central-block identities.
problems.depends: The height system H1–H4 on all required subproducts, source curves of correspondences and finite extensions; these arithmetic assertions are additional to height existence.

problems.title: Integral Northcott finiteness
problems.goal: Prove bounded-height finiteness for the projected images of integral cycles, first over a fixed field and then in bounded degree.
problems.formula: \(\#\{z\in\Lambda_{\le d}:q(z)\le B\}<\infty\). Here \(q\) is the signed residual quadratic height and \(\Lambda_{\le d}\) consists of projected integral classes defined over extensions of degree at most \(d\) of the fixed base field.
problems.method: Over each fixed field, combine real positivity with a common finite-rank lattice, or use real positivity and a proved height gap with a finite Kummer quotient for some integer m ≥ 2. Then bound ramification of the minimal fields of definition of bounded-height classes.
problems.output: A common finite-rank lattice and real positivity give fixed-field Northcott; the additional ramification control gives bounded-degree Northcott. Positive definiteness alone does not give either finiteness assertion.
problems.depends: The residual quadratic height and integral image from the arithmetic programme. Integral control and field control are separate requirements.

overview.title: Routes to Beilinson–Bloch height pairings
overview.summary: Three approaches to the existence problem. Each has its own account of the construction, known cases and remaining difficulties, with a separate mathematical article and PDF.
overview.context: Let \(X/F\) be smooth, projective and geometrically integral of dimension \(n\), over a number field. Write \(V^k(X)=\operatorname{CH}^k(X)_{\mathbb Q,\mathrm{hom}}\), where the subscript denotes geometric homological triviality, and let \(r+s=n+1\).

routes.title: Vanishing of local curvature obstructions
routes.summary: Start with the pairing on the common kernels of the local curvature maps. Prove that both kernels contain all homologically trivial classes.
routes.progress: Curvature correction, algebraic-equivalence vanishing and Chow-correspondence transfer give conditional constructions on the cycle groups and varieties listed in Progress.
routes.difficulty: Annihilate the curvature class of every localized global cycle, in both complementary codimensions.
routes.introduction: A prescribed cycle is first given a Green form with curvature. One then seeks a global primitive of that curvature. Since the curvature class depends only on the Chow class, algebraic equivalence and Chow correspondences become tools for proving its vanishing.
routes.conclusion: Under the analytic hypotheses, the construction gives \(h_X:\mathcal H^r(X)\times\mathcal H^s(X)\to\mathbb R\), where \(\mathcal H^k(X)\) is the common kernel of the curvature obstructions at all finite places. The constructed domain is the full product precisely when \(\mathcal H^r=V^r\) and \(\mathcal H^s=V^s\).

steps.title: A prescribed Green pair
steps.text: Construct \((G_Z,\Omega_Z)\) with \(D[G_Z]+\delta_Z=[\Omega_Z]\), where \(D=d'd''\). The actual Bott–Chern class \([\Omega_Z]=\mathfrak o([Z])\) must depend only on \([Z]\).

steps.title: Vanishing of the curvature class
steps.text: Prove \(\mathfrak o^k_{X_{F_v}}(z_{F_v})=0\) for every \(z\in V^k(X)\), every finite \(v\), and \(k=r,s\). For the global target, only localizations of global classes are needed.

steps.title: Removal of curvature
steps.kind: Proved deduction from the first two conditions
steps.text: Choose a global actual primitive \(D\Psi_Z=\Omega_Z\). Then \(\gamma_Z=G_Z-\Psi_Z\) on the prescribed complement has zero curvature. Stokes’ formula proves the Green identity against every actual complementary test.

steps.title: The global pairing
steps.text: The local intersection and principal-divisor identities give the pairing on the common kernels. The vanishing in Step 2 makes both of these kernels the full homologically trivial Chow groups.
steps.link: The global construction and its hypotheses

sections.title: Algebraic equivalence and Chow correspondences
sections.text: The compact-parameter argument annihilates the obstruction on algebraically trivial cycles. Covariance under rational Chow correspondences then transports vanishing. A decomposition of the diagonal reduces the problem to the varieties through which the diagonal factors. The analytic covariance and field-descent statements remain premises of these geometric deductions.

sections.title: Detection by periods
sections.text: One may seek fixed linear functionals \(P_1,\ldots,P_m\) with \(P_j(z)=0\) for every \(j\) implying \(\mathfrak o(z)=0\). This requires a comparison with the actual curvature obstruction and a vanishing theorem for those particular periods. Finite-dimensionality of a cohomology group alone is insufficient.

sections.title: The remaining problems
sections.text: The analytic foundation must establish the prescribed Green construction, trace and intersection identities on actual forms. Beyond the geometric cases, the central question is why homologically trivial Chow classes have zero image in Bott–Chern cohomology. After algebraically trivial classes have been killed, the remaining map factors through the corresponding quotient of the Chow group.

routes.title: Direct construction of zero-curvature Green forms
routes.summary: Construct strong Green forms directly, then prove the local identities needed to sum their pairings over all places.
routes.progress: The principal-divisor calculation and the product formula give a conditional passage from local Green forms to a global Chow pairing.
routes.difficulty: Construct actual Green forms with exact support and establish the restriction, trace and intersection identities used by the local height.
routes.status: Strong Green existence and analytic compatibility open in general
routes.introduction: This approach begins with a zero-curvature Green form itself, without requiring it to come from a particular Chern-character construction. The main additional task is to identify its integrals against principal cycles with the field norms describing rational equivalence.
routes.conclusion: At a finite place and for disjoint cycles, define \(\lambda_v(Z,W)=\int_{W_{F_v}^{\mathrm{an}}}\gamma_{Z,v}\); at infinity use the classical zero-curvature complex Green construction. Under the local calculus, moving and good-place hypotheses, the sum \(\sum_v [F_v:\mathbb Q_v]\lambda_v/[F:\mathbb Q]\) descends to \(V^r(X)\times V^s(X)\).

steps.title: Strong Green forms in both codimensions
steps.text: Over every original finite completion, construct \(\gamma_Z\in\mathcal B^{r-1,r-1}(X^{\mathrm{an}}\setminus|Z|^{\mathrm{an}})\) with \(\int\gamma_Z\wedge D\eta=-\int_Z\eta\) for all compactly supported actual complementary tests. Do the same in degree \(s\).

steps.title: Intersection and principal divisors
steps.text: Construct a principal-cycle Green form from −log|f| on a normal carrier. This uses a closed-immersion construction, a supported intersection formula and integration along a projective bundle, with their actual-form identities.

steps.title: The principal transformation law
steps.text: Reciprocity identifies the change under rational equivalence with \(-m^{-1}\log|a|_v\). One element \(a\in F^\times\) and one denominator \(m\), obtained from the algebraic norm calculation, must work at every place.

steps.title: Descent to Chow groups
steps.text: The weighted sum of the principal terms is zero. Moving cycles and applying the law in both variables gives a well-defined bilinear pairing; reciprocity gives symmetry. Good-place vanishing makes the sum finite.

sections.title: Tropical forms and global primitives
sections.text: One possible method is to solve for primitives on tropical charts and descend them to the Berkovich space. The comparison must preserve both differentials, integration and compatibility on overlaps. A topological inverse limit alone does not give this statement for forms. A global actual primitive, together with a prescribed curved Green pair, would supply a strong Green form.

sections.title: Descent to the original valued field
sections.text: For \(L/K\) finite, retain the extension of the original absolute value. A trace must be defined on the primitive, commute with \(D\), and satisfy adjunction on all actual tests. Descent uses the full factor \([L:K]^{-1}\). A proper alteration does not automatically supply a pushforward of arbitrary actual forms.

sections.title: The remaining problems
sections.text: The local existence problem retains the precise cycle complement, actual form sheaf and full test class. The principal-divisor argument also needs restriction along singular carriers and compatible projective-bundle integration. Correspondence adjunction and comparison with arithmetic-intersection heights require further identities with the same normalizations.

routes.title: Admissible arithmetic liftings: Zhang’s approach
routes.summary: Correct cycle closures by vertical cycles on arithmetic models, then use arithmetic intersection. The general construction follows conditionally from the standard conjectures.
routes.progress: Zhang proves a general conditional lifting theorem and constructs the pairing unconditionally for the product of a curve and a surface.
routes.difficulty: Prove the required duality and Lefschetz statements for algebraic classes on special fibres, or construct the necessary vertical corrections directly.
routes.status: Published conditional theorem; unconditional curve–surface case
routes.introduction: Shou-Wu Zhang’s construction uses algebraic cycle classes on the special fibres of arithmetic models. Vertical corrections make the closure of a homologically trivial cycle orthogonal to vertical cycles. Arithmetic intersection then gives a number independent of the chosen lifting.
routes.conclusion: For suitable liftings on a regular arithmetic model, \(h_X(z,w)=[F:\mathbb Q]^{-1}\widehat{\deg}(\widehat z\cdot\widehat w)\). A construction after alteration uses the corresponding degree-normalized descent.

steps.title: Algebraic classes on the special fibre
steps.text: For \(i:Y\hookrightarrow\mathcal X\), the image of \(i^*i_*:A_{n+1-r}(Y)\to A^r(Y)\) describes the curvature changes obtainable from vertical cycles. The local standard conjectures concern duality and Lefschetz operators on these groups. This local construction is made over the completion of a maximal unramified extension, with a geometric special fibre; return to the original place uses cycle descent.

steps.title: Harmonic decomposition and liftings
steps.text: The Lefschetz and Hodge standard conjectures on every smooth geometric stratum of a strictly semistable model imply local duality and Lefschetz. The harmonic curvature of a homologically trivial class is then zero. A vertical correction gives a Beilinson–Bloch lifting, and alterations extend the conditional lifting theorem to general reduction.

steps.title: Arithmetic intersection
steps.text: Combine the finite-place corrections with zero-curvature Green currents at infinity. Differences between liftings are vertical classes and zero-curvature archimedean terms. Orthogonality and homological triviality make their intersections with the complementary lifting vanish.

steps.title: Known cases and the general problem
steps.text: For a curve times a surface, Zhang verifies the required conditions on a semistable model and then uses alterations. In general, the corresponding standard conjectures, or a direct construction of the vertical correction, remain the substantial open input.

sections.title: The vertical correction equation
sections.text: For a closure \(\overline z\) of \(z\), seek a vertical class \(a\) satisfying \(i^*\overline z+i^*i_*a=0\) in the algebraic cohomology group. Numerical orthogonality is the condition needed by the intersection pairing; the cohomological lifting theorem supplies a sufficient correction.

sections.title: The product of a curve and a surface
sections.text: For \(X=C\times S\), with \(C\) a smooth projective curve and \(S\) a smooth projective surface over a number field, the middle pairing is on \(V^2(X)\times V^2(X)\). Zhang resolves the product of semistable models, checks the conditions on its strata and then passes to general reduction by alterations. This published result is separate from the conditional actual-form constructions.

sections.title: Relation to the Green-form approaches
sections.text: An arithmetic lifting and an actual non-Archimedean form are different objects. Comparing their heights requires equality of local intersection values with matching normalizations. Zhang’s L-liftings of all Chow classes are a further extension with additional arithmetic standard-conjecture hypotheses, not a premise of the ordinary homologically trivial pairing.
